/.h2: More questions about ordering custom poly mailers

faqs.q: What should a first brief for custom poly mailers include?
faqs.a: Three things are enough to start: what you ship, roughly how many, and which market it goes to. If you are unsure of the size or the film, say so, because working that out is part of the quotation rather than something you must settle first.

faqs.q: Which poly mailer decisions should be settled before artwork is designed?
faqs.a: Settle the size before the artwork and the color before the design. Artwork is laid out to a specific panel, so a later size change means redrawing it, and a color chosen after design changes how the ink reads on the film.

faqs.q: How are custom poly mailers checked during a production run?
faqs.a: Print is checked against your approved proof at the start, through and at the end of the run. Seals are checked along both welds, adhesive release is tested on pulled samples, and counts are verified by carton before dispatch.

faqs.q: Can I try poly mailer samples before committing to a full run?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the step we recommend most. Ask for two candidate sizes, pack your heaviest routine order into each, and choose the smaller one that closes without strain. Our poly mailer samples settle a size question faster than any chart.

faqs.q: Where should the shipping label go on a printed 10x13 mailer?
faqs.a: A standard four-by-six label covers a large share of the 10x13 front. Either leave a deliberate clear zone in the upper front sized for the label, or move the design to the reverse and keep the front plain so label placement no longer matters.

faqs.q: When does standardizing on a single 10x13 size stop making sense?
faqs.a: If more than about a fifth of your orders would sit awkwardly in a 10x13, either lost in it or straining it, the single-size case weakens quickly. Ranges where most orders are one or two garments are where it works best.

faqs.q: Can a 10x13 mailer take a thank-you card and insert?
faqs.a: Yes. The extra room a 10x13 has over a 9x12 is roughly what an A5 card, a sticker sheet and a returns slip take up, so mixed orders with an insert usually close without the seal working hard.

faqs.q: Is a chunky knit too bulky for a 10x13 poly mailer?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. A fine-gauge sweater fits a 10x13, but a chunky knit or a padded jacket does not, and forcing it puts the strain on the seal. Those items belong in a larger 12x15 poly mailer instead.

faqs.q: How should 10x13 poly mailers be stored between reorders?
faqs.a: Standardizing on 10x13 makes forecasting simple, because parcels shipped equals mailers used. Order to a run rate you can store properly, keeping cartons flat and dry so the film and adhesive strip stay in good condition.

faqs.q: Why do knitwear parcels in a tight mailer arrive open, unlike 12x15?
faqs.a: A chunky knit has loft and keeps pushing outward. In a mailer that is only just wide enough, the stretch concentrates at the seal and corners. A 12x15 gives the fold somewhere to go, so the bag stays flat and the seal lies on film.

faqs.q: Can a pair of jeans ship in a 12x15 poly mailer?
faqs.a: Yes. A single pair of jeans folds into a 12x15 without straining the closure. Denim and knitwear also carry high return rates, which is why a second adhesive strip is often worth quoting at this size.

faqs.q: Does moving up to 12x15 mailers change shipping costs?
faqs.a: It can. Weigh a packed 12x15 sample before committing, because a size change can push a parcel across a carrier pricing threshold and wipe out the saving you expected. Cartons also hold fewer units, so reorder points arrive sooner.

faqs.q: Does full-coverage print work well on a 12x15 mailer?
faqs.a: A 12x15 is the smallest size where a full-coverage design reads properly at arm's length. The trade-off is that large solid areas show any inconsistency in ink lay-down, so ask for a solid brand color to be reviewed at proof stage.

faqs.q: Which film weight suits 12x15 poly mailers for heavier contents?
faqs.a: Heavier film is the usual choice at 12x15 because the contents tend to be heavier too: knitwear, denim and multi-garment bundles. The exact film weight for your order is confirmed in writing on the quotation.

faqs.q: How do I decide between 10x13 and 12x15 when between sizes?
faqs.a: Use the thickest order you send regularly, not the average one. If that order compresses in a 10x13 or leaves the seal working hard, the 12x15 is the safer standard. Testing both sizes with a real packed order settles it quickly.

faqs.q: Why do 14.5x19 mailers tear at the corners in transit?
faqs.a: The failure on large mailers is almost always movement rather than film strength. A heavy item in a 14.5x19 bag with slack air around it swings, and swinging tears corners. Fold to the shape of the bag and press the air out as you seal.

faqs.q: Can light outerwear be shipped in a 14.5x19 poly mailer?
faqs.a: Yes. Packable jackets, gilets and shells folded down are one of the main uses of 14.5x19, along with fleece-lined and oversized hoodies that will not close in a 12x15. Fold them into a rectangle that matches the bag.

faqs.q: Do soft goods in a 14.5x19 mailer need extra tape?
faqs.a: Soft goods do not need tape. A boxed item inside a 14.5x19 does, because a corner concentrates the whole load in one place. Reinforce only when the contents are hard, and keep the adhesive strip on a clean run of film.

faqs.q: Where should the label sit on a 14.5x19 poly mailer?
faqs.a: Place it on a flat face. A label across a fold or a bulge lifts at the edges, and a lifted label causes scanning failures and delivery exceptions. Packing the garment to a neat rectangle creates that flat face.

faqs.q: Is heavier film recommended for every 14.5x19 poly mailer order?
faqs.a: At 14.5x19 the heavier option is the default recommendation rather than an upgrade, because contents such as hoodies and outerwear bundles weigh more. Outerwear ranges also see high return rates, so a second strip is often worth quoting.

faqs.q: How should a packing bench store 14.5x19 mailer stock?
faqs.a: Large mailers come in fewer units per carton and take more bench space. Most operations keep a small working stock of 14.5x19 near the bench and hold the rest sealed, because film left open in a warm room picks up dust on the adhesive.

faqs.q: Can 19x24 poly mailers handle wholesale drops to a stockist?
faqs.a: Yes. A small soft-goods assortment going to one retail account is a typical 19x24 use, travelling without the cost or weight of a carton and void fill. Anything that needs packaging to hold a shape should still go in a box.

faqs.q: How should weight be spread inside a 19x24 poly mailer?
faqs.a: Spread the load evenly across the whole footprint so pressure is shared and the parcel stays flat. The same weight concentrated in one corner of a 19x24 becomes a pendulum, and a pendulum finds the weakest point of the seal.

faqs.q: Are 19x24 mailers suitable for consolidating store returns?
faqs.a: They are a common choice for moving batched returns from a store or hub back to a central site. A resealable closure saves a second piece of packaging, and printed instructions reduce the number of parcels that come back wrongly packed.

faqs.q: Why is the lightest film not quoted for 19x24 mailers?
faqs.a: The loads that go into a 19x24, such as bedding sets, consolidated orders and wholesale drops, do not suit the lightest film. Larger formats put more strain on every part of the bag, so film weight matters more here.

faqs.q: Does consolidating orders into one 19x24 mailer always save money?
faqs.a: Not automatically. A consolidated parcel can cross a weight or size threshold that two smaller parcels stayed below. Weigh and measure a realistically packed 19x24 sample before moving a whole order flow across.

faqs.q: Is full-coverage printing worth it on a 19x24 mailer?
faqs.a: For wholesale and returns use, rarely. A clear mark and handling wording usually does the job on a 19x24. Full coverage makes more sense if the bag reaches end customers who will see it at the door.

faqs.q: When is a 24x24 square mailer the wrong choice?
faqs.a: For long, thin items. A rolled poster or a folded curtain in a 24x24 leaves two large empty triangles, and empty space in a flexible parcel lets contents move. A rectangular format at the right proportion protects better and costs less.

faqs.q: Can pet beds and blankets ship in a 24x24 mailer?
faqs.a: Yes. Soft pet beds, mats and blankets compress but spring back into a rounded square, which suits a 24x24 footprint. Build the load out to the corners rather than leaving it in the middle of the bag.

faqs.q: How do I seal a 24x24 mailer with lofty contents?
faqs.a: Lofty contents rise as you fold the flap. Press down evenly across the whole face, then hold the load down while sealing so the adhesive strip meets clean film rather than the contents underneath.

faqs.q: Which face of a 24x24 mailer should carry the label?
faqs.a: On a square parcel both faces look alike, so choose the flatter one deliberately. Keep that face free of artwork if the label must scan reliably, and put the design on the other side.

faqs.q: Why do lofty contents rule out light film on 24x24 mailers?
faqs.a: Lofty contents such as cushion inserts and folded quilts keep the film under constant tension. At 24x24 that tension is spread over a large face, so the lighter film weights are not quoted for this size.

faqs.q: Does matte or gloss suit a printed 24x24 mailer better?
faqs.a: Matte is usually the better choice on a 24x24, because it reduces the visible creasing that lofty contents cause across a large face. The finish for your order is confirmed in writing on your quotation.

faqs.q: Can jewelry be shipped safely in a 6x9 poly mailer?
faqs.a: Yes. Boxed earrings, chains, hair clips and pins are typical 6x9 contents, usually with a card and tissue wrap. Heavier film helps resist puncture from a hard-cornered item such as a boxed watch.

faqs.q: How should a logo be laid out on a 6x9 mailer?
faqs.a: Treat the 6x9 front as a single element: one mark, sized generously, with clear space around it. Move the web address, social handles and care wording to the reverse, where no closure strip competes for room.

faqs.q: Will fine script logos print clearly on a 6x9 mailer?
faqs.a: Fine lines can close up on flexible film in a way they never do on paper, and the small 6x9 panel makes it worse. Ask for thin scripts, hairline rules or tight monograms to be checked at proof stage before the run.

faqs.q: Is a tear tab worth adding to 6x9 gift mailers?
faqs.a: For gift ranges it often is. A tear tab lets the recipient open a 6x9 bag without scissors, which matters when the contents are small items such as jewelry or beauty singles meant to feel like a present.

faqs.q: Why do sellers often order too many 6x9 mailers?
faqs.a: Sellers with a mix of small items and folded apparel often buy 6x9 first as a starting point, then find anything thicker than a folded t-shirt will not close. Most run 6x9 alongside a 9x12 poly mailer size.

faqs.q: Do 6x9 poly mailers work for prints and sticker packs?
faqs.a: Yes. Flat paper goods such as print orders, sticker packs, enamel-pin cards and greetings ranges are a good fit for 6x9, because a close fit stops them sliding and bending so they arrive uncreased.

faqs.q: How do I test a 9x12 mailer before ordering a run?
faqs.a: Pack your heaviest realistic order the way packers actually fold, seal it and check the strip meets clean film, drop it once flat from bench height, then weigh it against your shipping bands. Ten minutes with a sample prevents a costly mistake.

faqs.q: When is 9x12 a better choice than 10x13?
faqs.a: When your average order is genuinely one thin garment. A 9x12 wastes less film per parcel and stacks more tightly in a carton, and across thousands of orders those savings compound in a way the larger size cannot match.

faqs.q: What artwork mistakes are common on 9x12 poly mailers?
faqs.a: The common ones are printing to the very edge without a bleed allowance, placing the logo where the shipping label goes, and assuming the stated size includes the flap. Each is easy to avoid once spotted at proof stage.

faqs.q: Is two-sided printing worth it on a 9x12 mailer?
faqs.a: 9x12 is the smallest size where two-sided print earns its cost. The front carries the mark, and the reverse carries what customers read at the door, such as how to return an item and where to find you.

faqs.q: When should a brand move up from 9x12 mailers?
faqs.a: When orders regularly include two garments, a knitted item, or a garment plus a substantial insert. They may still close in a 9x12, but the seal ends up doing work it was not designed for, and that is the point to move up.

faqs.q: Does opacity matter for dark garments in a 9x12 mailer?
faqs.a: Yes. Higher opacity matters when the contents are dark and the mailer is pale, because otherwise the garment can show through the film. Opacity is one of the variables confirmed on your 9x12 quotation.

faqs.a: One product category in many configurations: size-specific, colored, printed, blank, padded, cushioned and self-seal poly mailers, plus frosted zip-closure garment bags. We do not present ourselves as a general packaging supplier, and every order is made to a written specification.

/apparel-shipping-bags/.h2: More questions about apparel shipping bags

faqs.q: How should I test apparel shipping bag sizes with my team?
faqs.a: Test with your own packers, at pace, on a normal day. A garment folded carefully at a desk fits a size that the same garment folded at speed does not, and that gap is where apparel bag sizing goes wrong.

faqs.q: Is it worth writing down a standard fold for apparel shipping bags?
faqs.a: Yes. A consistent fold across a team makes parcel size predictable, which makes shipping costs predictable and lets packed apparel parcels stack neatly instead of sprawling across the bench.

faqs.q: How can a packing team identify bagged garments without opening apparel mailers?
faqs.a: Color coding or a printed panel on the apparel shipping bag solves it cheaply. Operations handling many similar bagged garments can then identify size or style at a glance without opening each parcel.

faqs.q: How do I work out which apparel shipping bag sizes to stock?
faqs.a: Take your five most-shipped items, pack each as a real order with the insert and returns slip, and group them. They usually cluster naturally into two or three sizes, which most garment operations settle on.

faqs.q: Can several apparel shipping bag sizes be ordered on one run?
faqs.a: Yes. Running two or three sizes together shares setup where the specification and artwork match, and ordering them together keeps the color and print consistent across the range. Settle the sizes before the artwork is drawn.

/artwork-guidelines/.h2: More questions about poly mailer artwork files

faqs.q: Why should poly mailer artwork avoid the flap and side welds?
faqs.a: The top band folds over and is sealed, so anything placed there is invisible on a packed parcel. The side edges are sealed and pinched, and artwork running into those welds distorts.

faqs.q: Should fonts be outlined in artwork files for poly mailer printing?
faqs.a: Yes. Live fonts substitute silently if we do not hold exactly the same version, which can change your type without anyone noticing. Outline them, and include a flattened preview so we can see what you intended.

faqs.q: Which checks are run when poly mailer artwork arrives?
faqs.a: Five: a technical check of format, resolution, color mode, bleed and line weights; a layout check for flap, welds and label zone; a contrast check against the film; then a proof; then written approval before scheduling.

faqs.q: Which artwork file types does the poly mailer quote form accept?
faqs.a: The quote form accepts PDF, AI, EPS, PSD, SVG, PNG and JPG files. They are checked on upload and attached to the inquiry rather than stored on a public path. If a file is over the upload limit, send a link instead.

faqs.q: Do I need commercial rights to artwork printed on poly mailers?
faqs.a: Yes. Stock illustration on a personal license, an image found online and a paid freelance design are three different legal positions, and only one is safe to print at volume. Fonts carry licenses too, some restricting packaging use.

/australia/.h2: More questions about poly mailers for Australia

faqs.q: How should an Australian business plan a poly mailer order date?
faqs.a: Work from a date, not a duration. Fix when stock must be on your bench in Australia, then work backwards through production and proof approval. We confirm the schedule in writing with the critical path identified.

faqs.q: Why keep plain poly mailer stock as a fallback in Australia?
faqs.a: Distance makes lead time a real planning input for Australian buyers. Holding some plain stock means a delayed printed run never stops orders leaving, and holding a buffer costs less than being unable to ship.

faqs.q: How does the southern calendar affect Australian poly mailer orders?
faqs.a: Peak retail in Australia arrives with summer, so seasonal stock is ordered in the quietest part of the year and held through the warmest weeks, when closure adhesive ages fastest. Storage conditions matter more as a result.

faqs.q: Are import charges shown on Australian poly mailer quotations?
faqs.a: Documentation and charges for an Australian order are stated on the quotation, before you commit. Quotations for Australian customers are issued in Australian dollars, alongside the written schedule for your order.

faqs.q: When should an Australian business reorder custom poly mailers?
faqs.a: Reorder at a stock level rather than on a calendar date, so the trigger reflects actual usage. Given the distance involved, set that level high enough to cover production, proofing and freight to your Australian address.

faqs.q: Which Australian cities are covered in your poly mailer guides?
faqs.a: Separate guides cover Sydney, Brisbane, Adelaide, Melbourne and Perth, each on a different commercial situation, such as long freight legs or environmental claims. Read the Brisbane seasonal planning guide for the reversed calendar.

/bee-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about bee poly mailers

faqs.q: Why do bee poly mailers suit year-round use for small makers?
faqs.a: Bee and botanical patterns read as seasonal without belonging to a season, so the same parcel works in March and October. That avoids the dead stock risk that comes with packaging tied to one selling window.

faqs.q: Should I start with a stock bee pattern or commission my own?
faqs.a: A sensible sequence is to run a stock bee pattern first, find out whether customers respond to it, then commission your own once you know. The difference is cost, timing and whether anyone else can have the same parcel.

faqs.q: Which businesses typically order bee poly mailers?
faqs.a: Honey and apiary producers, garden and seed sellers, handmade and craft makers, natural skincare brands and stationery or gift ranges. For each, a bee or botanical pattern matches what the products are already saying.

faqs.q: Does a tinted base help a bee poly mailer pattern?
faqs.a: A tinted base under a bee pattern reads warmer than white and hides handling marks better. Pattern scale is set against the chosen size, so settle the mailer size before finalizing the pattern.

faqs.q: Is a simpler bee pattern cheaper at low volumes?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Color count affects setup cost, so a bee pattern with fewer colors is cheaper on a small run. A clear label panel within the pattern also keeps the shipping label legible and adhering properly.

faqs.q: Why does a repeat pattern like bee artwork survive packing well?
faqs.a: A logo has a right place on a bag and can end up folded or under a label. A bee repeat pattern has no wrong place, so it still works however the parcel is packed, sealed and labeled.

/biodegradable-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about biodegradable poly mailer claims

faqs.q: Why does the word biodegradable on its own mean so little?
faqs.a: Almost everything breaks down eventually. Without named conditions and a timeframe, biodegradable describes a property every material has, and tells a customer nothing about what will actually happen to the mailer.

faqs.q: Can a biodegradable mailer behave differently in landfill?
faqs.a: Yes. Biodegradation depends on temperature, moisture, oxygen and microbial activity. A film that breaks down in warm, wet, oxygen-rich conditions may sit unchanged for decades in landfill, where oxygen is scarce and conditions are stable.

faqs.q: What four questions should a biodegradable mailer claim answer?
faqs.a: Under what conditions, how completely, over what period, and assessed by whom against which method. If a supplier cannot answer all four for the specific film, the biodegradable claim is not one you should print.

faqs.q: Is fragmentation the same as a mailer biodegrading?
faqs.a: No. Fragmentation means the film breaks into smaller pieces rather than breaking down fully, and it is a specific concern with some additive-based films. Ask any supplier of biodegradable film which one their evidence actually shows.

faqs.q: How are biodegradable poly mailers described on your quotation?
faqs.a: The material is quoted using the film supplier's own description, attributed to them rather than restated as our claim. If nothing is documented, the quotation says so plainly, and you see that before you order biodegradable mailers.

/black-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about black poly mailers

faqs.q: Can I write a handwritten note on a black poly mailer?
faqs.a: Not practically. Pen does not show on a black poly mailer, so a handwritten note on the bag is not an option. Put a printed or handwritten card inside the parcel instead.

faqs.q: Will a white shipping label stand out on black mailers?
faqs.a: Yes. Labels adhere fine, but a small white label on a large black parcel is a very visible rectangle. Decide where the label goes as part of the design rather than letting packers place it anywhere.

faqs.q: Can a brand with a black wordmark use black poly mailers?
faqs.a: Not as it stands. White is the only ink that reads reliably on black at every size, pale metallics work only at larger sizes, and a dark wordmark simply disappears. A reversed white version is the usual answer.

faqs.q: How should artwork be supplied for a black poly mailer run?
faqs.a: As a single-color file: a white mark on a transparent background gives us exactly what is needed without interpretation. Print it at actual size on paper first, because fine lines can close up on film.

faqs.q: Can black match across plain and bubble-lined poly mailers?
faqs.a: Black carries across both constructions so a mixed range still looks like a set, but plain film and a cushioned surface reflect differently. Matching the depth of black needs a check at proof stage, as covered in our printed bubble mailer options.

faqs.q: Does film weight matter for opacity on black poly mailers?
faqs.a: Not for opacity, because black is already fully opaque. On a black poly mailer, film weight is about strength and puncture resistance, so choose it against what you ship rather than to stop show-through.

/blank-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about blank poly mailers

faqs.q: How can I brand a blank poly mailer without printing it?
faqs.a: Choose a colored film, add a printed sticker or seal, put the design inside on a card or tissue, standardize label placement, and include a printed returns insert. None of these needs print setup, and all can change tomorrow.

faqs.q: When is it time to switch from blank to printed poly mailers?
faqs.a: Three signals usually arrive together: volume becomes predictable enough to forecast a run, the artwork stops changing, and customers start photographing parcels. When all three are true, printing pays for itself quickly.

faqs.q: Are blank poly mailers suitable for third-party fulfillment work?
faqs.a: Yes. Third-party fulfillment and multi-brand sellers cannot put one logo on every parcel, so blank stock is often the correct product. A resealable blank mailer is also a common choice for fulfillment operations.

faqs.q: Does moving from blank to printed poly mailers change the specification?
faqs.a: No. The size, film and closure stay the same and only the artwork is added. Most businesses run down existing blank stock while the first printed run is proofed, so there is no gap in supply.

faqs.q: Can several sizes of blank poly mailers go on one order?
faqs.a: Yes. Blank orders are the easiest place to run several sizes together, because there is no artwork to lay out for each panel. Color, finish, film weight and closure are all still selectable on a blank order.

faqs.q: Should a first printed run follow blank poly mailers with full coverage?
faqs.a: There is no need. A single printed mark on a colored film is a low-cost first printed run after blank mailers, and it shows what customers respond to before you commit to something more elaborate.

/blog/choosing-colors-for-branded-shippi.h2: More questions on choosing mailer colors

faqs.q: Why does the same blush mailer look different in photos?
faqs.a: Pale tones pick up the color of whatever surface they are photographed on, which is why the same blush mailer can look peach on wood and mauve on gray. Matte reads evenly under most light, while gloss produces hotspots.

faqs.q: Which inks read on a black or charcoal shipping mailer?
faqs.a: Black and charcoal accept white and pale metallics and very little else. They are fully opaque and hide marks almost completely, but the narrow ink range rules out any dark mark, whatever the print quality.

faqs.q: Is gray or silver a good color for branded shipping mailers?
faqs.a: The guide calls gray and silver an underrated middle ground. They hide handling marks well, accept dark inks and white as a solid, and read neutral rather than making a statement on the doorstep.

faqs.q: Why are deep jewel tones a useful shipping mailer color?
faqs.a: Deep jewel tones read as premium, hide marks well, and take white and pale metallics. They are often the most useful compromise between a black that feels severe and a bright that feels promotional.

faqs.q: Should mailer color or printing carry the brand identity?
faqs.a: Decide that first. If the color does the work, choose it for doorstep recognition and you may not need printing at all. If print does the work, choose the mailer color for contrast against your ink instead.

faqs.q: Can mailer colors be used to organize a packing operation?
faqs.a: Yes. The guide treats color as an operational tool: different mailer colors can separate order types or ranges at a glance, so packers and handlers can tell parcels apart without reading the label or opening the bag.

faqs.q: What are the risks of pastel colors for shipping mailers?
faqs.a: Blush and pastels give the softest read but are the most demanding technically. They take dark inks only, show-through of dark contents is a real risk, and marks show more than on any base except white.

/blog/how-custom-printed-poly-mailers-su.h2: More questions on printed mailers and brand recognition

faqs.q: What does a printed poly mailer do that a plain one cannot?
faqs.a: Three things at once: it is identified on the doorstep before it is opened, it gives customers something worth photographing, and it signals care before the product is seen. Printing does the second most reliably of all.

faqs.q: When is it too early to invest in printed poly mailers?
faqs.a: Until volume stops swinging, artwork stops changing and customers photograph the parcel. Printing commits artwork, size, color and quantity at once, so before those three conditions hold, colored stock with a printed seal sticker delivers most of the recognition.

faqs.q: Which design approach works best for brand recognition on mailers?
faqs.a: Restraint. A mailer is seen packed, folded and labeled, not flat. Fewer elements, larger, survive: one idea sized generously, a wordmark that reads across a room, and a single strong color rather than a subtle palette.

faqs.q: Which artwork details get lost on a printed poly mailer?
faqs.a: Fine line work, small type, tonal gradients and anything placed where the flap folds over or the shipping label lands. At the distance a parcel is actually viewed, small detail becomes texture rather than branding.

faqs.q: How can a brand get recognition from a small print budget?
faqs.a: A strong colored film achieves doorstep recognition, a printed seal sticker carries the mark, and something considered inside the bag signals care. Together they deliver much of what a printed run does for a fraction of the commitment.

faqs.q: Why should brand mailer artwork plan for the shipping label?
faqs.a: A four-by-six label covers a large share of a mid-size mailer's front panel and lands wherever the packer finds space. Design a clear zone for it, or put the artwork on the reverse and keep the front plain.

faqs.q: Is a printed mailer a packaging or a marketing purchase?
faqs.a: The article argues it is a marketing decision dressed as a procurement one. Bought as packaging, the question is cost per unit. Bought as a marketing surface, the question is what it does that the same spend elsewhere would not.

/blog/how-to-choose-the-right-poly-maile.h2: More questions on choosing poly mailer sizes

faqs.q: Why is packed depth the key poly mailer sizing measurement?
faqs.a: Depth decides whether the bag closes properly and which shipping band the parcel lands in. A parcel small in footprint but thick in section often costs more to send than a wider, flatter one holding the same things.

faqs.q: Should I measure the product or the packed order when sizing?
faqs.a: The packed order. A folded t-shirt is not what you ship; you ship it with a card, stickers, a returns slip and perhaps a sample, compressed by someone working quickly. That bundle is what has to fit the mailer.

faqs.q: How many poly mailer samples should I test when sizing?
faqs.a: Ask for two candidate sizes rather than one, because the comparison is what produces the answer. Pack your heaviest routine order into each, seal it, drop it, and weigh it against your shipping bands.

faqs.q: How do I drop-test a poly mailer size before ordering?
faqs.a: Drop each packed parcel once, flat, from bench height onto a hard floor, then once on a corner. A seal that opens on a single drop will open in a sorting hub, which means the size or seal is wrong.

faqs.q: Why is sizing up a poly mailer not the safer choice?
faqs.a: Extra room lets contents move, gather speed and hit the ends of the bag, which damages corners and opens seals. A larger mailer also uses more film and can push a parcel into a higher shipping band.

faqs.q: Which products should I use to choose my poly mailer sizes?
faqs.a: Your five most-shipped products rather than the whole catalog. Five usually cover the large majority of volume, and they tend to cluster into two or three sizes without forcing, often matching our standard poly mailer sizes.

faqs.q: How do I know a poly mailer is too tight when sealing?
faqs.a: Check that the adhesive strip meets clean film along its whole length. If the contents reach the strip anywhere, that part of the seal is bonded to the product rather than the bag, and it is where the parcel will open.

/blog/how-to-prepare-artwork-for-custom-.h2: More questions on preparing poly mailer artwork

faqs.q: Which decisions must come before designing poly mailer artwork?
faqs.a: Four: the size, settled on a physical sample; the base color, which decides which inks will read; the finish, because matte and gloss change how ink reads; and the coverage, which is the budget conversation.

faqs.q: Can a 10x13 mailer design simply be scaled to 12x15?
faqs.a: No. Artwork is laid out for a specific panel, and the proportions of the printable area differ between sizes once the flap and welds are accounted for. A size change means redrawing the layout rather than rescaling it.

faqs.q: Why design poly mailer artwork at final printed size?
faqs.a: Working at the dimensions the bag will actually be means type sizes and line weights are judged at real scale. Artwork scaled up at the end often reveals details that are too fine or type that is too small.

faqs.q: Should dead zones be marked on a poly mailer artwork template?
faqs.a: Yes. Draw the flap area and the weld margins on your template and keep anything important out of both. Seeing these zones while designing is far more reliable than trying to remember them.

faqs.q: Why should poly mailer artwork use CMYK or a spot color?
faqs.a: An RGB file has to be converted for print, and the conversion is where unexpected color shifts come from. Setting CMYK or a named spot color yourself means you see the result rather than leaving the decision to the printer.

faqs.q: How should I use the proof for my poly mailer artwork?
faqs.a: Check placement, scale, spelling, your web address and social handles, because once approved they are what gets printed. Where a brand color matters commercially, check it physically, since a screen is backlit and film is not.

faqs.q: Why do artwork problems on poly mailers usually happen?
faqs.a: Most are sequencing problems rather than design problems. The file is fine, but it was made before a decision that constrains it, such as size or base color. Getting the order right removes most reasons for a second proof round.

/blog/packaging-ideas-for-small-ecommerc.h2: More packaging questions for small ecommerce businesses

faqs.q: What do customers notice first about a small ecommerce parcel?
faqs.a: Color, cleanliness and care. A colored bag sealed neatly with a straight label reads better than an elaborate printed one sealed carelessly. Two of those three things are free, and a colored stock mailer covers the third.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest upgrade for small ecommerce packaging?
faqs.a: A colored film instead of white. It is a small premium over the cheapest option and the largest single change available, making a parcel recognizable on a doorstep with no artwork, no proof and no commitment.

faqs.q: Why should a small ecommerce brand put branding inside the bag?
faqs.a: A card, folded note or tissue in a matching tone is what gets photographed and what people keep, and it is the cheapest element to reprint. It carries the brand without fixing anything on the mailer itself.

faqs.q: Why should a small ecommerce business avoid buying a year of packaging?
faqs.a: The discount is real, and so is the risk. Adhesive ages, ranges change and order profiles shift, so a year of stock can be outgrown within months. Ordering a quantity you will use in a season keeps you flexible.

faqs.q: What should a small ecommerce business learn from its first hundred parcels?
faqs.a: Look at which size ran out, what arrived damaged and what customers mentioned. That is real data about your packaging, and it beats any prediction made before the first order shipped.

faqs.q: Is matte finish worth it for small ecommerce mailers?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Matte costs a small premium over gloss, photographs better and hides handling marks. For a small ecommerce business it is one of the cheaper ways to make plain packaging look considered.

faqs.q: How should a small ecommerce business order its first mailers?
faqs.a: Request samples in two sizes, then buy one size, plain, in a color, and brand it with a sticker. Order a season's quantity, ship a hundred parcels, and print only once volume and artwork have settled. Start with poly mailer samples.

/blog/poly-mailer-thickness-and-durabili.h2: More questions on poly mailer thickness

faqs.q: Why do microns and mils confuse poly mailer thickness comparisons?
faqs.a: Converting between microns and mils is trivial. The harder part is noticing that one supplier quoted a target thickness while another quoted a minimum, and that difference matters more than the unit conversion.

faqs.q: Is mailer thickness measured on flat film or the finished bag?
faqs.a: It can be either, and they describe different things. The gap between a flat-film figure and a finished-bag figure is not a constant you can adjust for, so ask both suppliers which one they quoted.

faqs.q: Which mailer failure does a heavier film actually prevent?
faqs.a: Film weight matters for one failure mode: puncture and tear from concentrated force, such as a hard corner or zip. It does nothing for crushing, poor fit or a badly pressed seal, which cause many transit failures.

faqs.q: How does sealing technique affect poly mailer durability?
faqs.a: A strip that was folded rather than pressed produces a partial bond that survives the bench and opens in a sorting hub. More film weight does not compensate for this at all, so seal technique deserves training.

faqs.q: Does storage affect poly mailer durability before use?
faqs.a: Yes. Heat, humidity and sunlight age the adhesive closure long before they affect the film, and a carton that has sat in a warm room for a year seals noticeably worse. Store mailers flat, cool and dry.

faqs.q: What should I ask a supplier about poly mailer film weight?
faqs.a: Ask which contents the film is recommended for, what the next weight up changes, whether the figure is a target or minimum, whether it was measured on film or bag, and what happens if the film becomes unavailable.

faqs.q: Can two films with the same thickness perform differently?
faqs.a: Yes. How the film was produced, what it is blended from and how the seals were formed all affect whether a bag survives a drop. Two films of identical stated thickness can behave noticeably differently in use.

/blog/poly-mailers-for-clothing-and-appa.h2: More questions on shipping clothing in poly mailers

faqs.q: What poly mailer size suits jeans and fine-gauge knitwear?
faqs.a: A 12x15 is the sensible starting point for jeans and fine-gauge knitwear, including a card and returns slip. The extra depth of the size matters more for these garments than the extra footprint.

faqs.q: Which poly mailer size suits leggings and swimwear?
faqs.a: A 10x13 handles leggings, swimwear and light bottoms, and firmly so if two-item orders are common. Lighter single items may fit a smaller bag, but a 10x13 leaves room for inserts without straining the seal.

faqs.q: What poly mailer size fits socks and underwear orders?
faqs.a: A 6x9 handles socks, underwear and small accessories comfortably for a single-item order. Move up a size if a typical order includes several pairs or a larger insert alongside the garments.

faqs.q: Which clothing mailer size matters most to keep in stock?
faqs.a: The largest one. It handles only a small share of orders, but it generates damage claims when it is missing, because the alternative is forcing a coat into a bag built for a tee.

faqs.q: Why does a black mailer suit many clothing brands?
faqs.a: A dark base color removes the show-through question completely, because a dark garment cannot shadow through black film. Higher-opacity or heavier film can also solve it on paler colors if quoted against your range.

faqs.q: Why do clothing mailers need to plan for returns?
faqs.a: Fashion return rates are the highest in retail, so a meaningful share of what you send comes back. Packaging chosen only for the outbound journey makes the inbound one more expensive than it needs to be.

faqs.q: Do wholesale and direct clothing orders need different mailers?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. The same range often ships one item to a customer and many to a stockist, which needs a second, larger size rather than a compromise on the first. Our 19x24 poly mailers suit consolidated drops.

/blog/poly-mailers-vs-padded-mailers/.h2: More questions on poly versus padded mailers

faqs.q: Which four failure modes decide poly versus padded mailers?
faqs.a: Impact, abrasion, crushing and movement. Only impact is what a bubble lining is built for; abrasion needs foam or separation, crushing needs a rigid carton, and movement needs a smaller bag. Look at how items broke before choosing.

faqs.q: Does a plain poly mailer keep contents dry in rain?
faqs.a: Polyethylene does not absorb water, so a parcel left on a doorstep in rain usually arrives with dry contents, provided the closure was sealed properly. The closure is where most water actually gets in.

faqs.q: Do t-shirts need a padded mailer instead of a plain poly mailer?
faqs.a: No. A folded garment is its own cushioning, and a knitted item absorbs impact better than most linings. Buying padding for a t-shirt is paying for protection against a failure that cannot happen.

faqs.q: When is a padded mailer worth more than a plain poly mailer?
faqs.a: For boxed items where the carton is part of the product, fragile items that are boxed first, hard corners in a mixed parcel, and contents where a failure costs a replacement, a reshipment and a customer's future orders.

faqs.q: Why does a padded mailer not stop crushed contents?
faqs.a: A flexible bag has no structure, so a load applied on top passes straight through whatever lining is inside. Deformed or flattened contents point to a rigid carton, not to a thicker padded mailer.

faqs.q: Why might upgrading to padded mailers not reduce damage?
faqs.a: If the real failure is abrasion, crushing or movement, padding does not address it. Some businesses upgrade twice without the damage rate improving because they bought cushioning for a failure mode that was not the problem.

faqs.q: Can an unboxed mug ship safely in a padded mailer?
faqs.a: Poorly. Cushioning works across a face, and a mug presents an edge. A padded mailer protects a boxed ceramic well, so box fragile items first and then use the cushioned mailer around the box.

/blog/recycled-vs-compostable-vs-biodegr.h2: More questions on recycled, compostable and biodegradable mailers

faqs.q: What is post-consumer recycled content in a mailer?
faqs.a: Material recovered after it was used and discarded by a household or business. It is the feedstock that actually diverts waste from disposal, and it is what most buyers assume they are getting when a supplier says recycled.

faqs.q: How is post-industrial recycled content different from post-consumer?
faqs.a: Post-industrial material is offcuts, trim and rejects recovered inside a manufacturing process before reaching anyone. It is legitimately recycled, but it was never headed for landfill, so the environmental argument is considerably weaker.

faqs.q: Why are most recycled-content mailer films blended with virgin polymer?
faqs.a: Recycled feedstock alone affects how film runs and performs, so a proportion of recycled material combined with virgin polymer is the usual arrangement. A meaningful claim names the feedstock and the proportion, traced to a document.

faqs.q: Why do compostable mailer programs often fail in practice?
faqs.a: A brand buys the material and prints the word, but the customer has no access to a composting facility, so the bag goes into general waste. The benefit does not happen, and the claim is not supported by the outcome.

faqs.q: What is the difference between industrial and home composting for mailers?
faqs.a: Industrial composting happens at a facility built to hold sustained temperature, moisture and oxygen; home composting happens in a domestic heap at much lower temperatures. A material can be assessed for one and not the other.

faqs.q: Which of the three mailer terms is easiest to evidence?
faqs.a: Recycled content, because the evidence exists at the point of manufacture and does not depend on anything a customer does afterwards. Biodegradable is the hardest, which should shape which one you build a customer promise around.

faqs.q: What should a brand ask before choosing a compostable mailer route?
faqs.a: What your customers can actually access, what you will tell them to do with the bag, and what documentation exists for the specific material. Our compostable poly mailer guide states which of those we can answer.

/blog/when-to-use-bubble-lined-poly-mail.h2: More questions on bubble-lined poly mailers

faqs.q: Why does a small item in a large bubble mailer still break?
faqs.a: Protection only exists where the lining sits between the contents and the outside. A small item in a large bubble mailer slides and accelerates, and the lining at the end of the bag must absorb a much bigger impact than intended.

faqs.q: Are smaller bubbles in a bubble-lined mailer ever better?
faqs.a: Bubble size is a trade rather than an upgrade. Smaller bubbles spread smaller forces more evenly and keep the parcel thinner, while larger bubbles absorb bigger single impacts but add bulk to the packed parcel.

faqs.q: Do bubble-lined poly mailers suit boxed cosmetics and electronics?
faqs.a: Yes, this is where they most often pay. The lining protects the retail carton, and a crushed box is a customer complaint even when the product inside is fine. Our beauty and cosmetics mailer guide covers this.

faqs.q: Do bubble-lined mailers stop scratches on shipped items?
faqs.a: No. Scratched and scuffed surfaces mean things are rubbing, and bubble absorbs impact rather than preventing abrasion. Foam is designed for that, and separating touching surfaces prevents it entirely.

faqs.q: Are bubble-lined mailers worth it for multi-leg shipping routes?
faqs.a: Often. Consolidation, transfers and long multi-leg routes each add handling and impact opportunities that a single-leg local delivery does not have, so parcels handled repeatedly are one case where a bubble lining earns its cost.

faqs.q: What is often a better fix than adding a bubble lining?
faqs.a: A closer fit. If damage is inconsistent and contents rattle, the bag is too big, and a smaller plain mailer will outperform a larger cushioned one while costing less. The most effective change is often free.

faqs.q: How do I tell whether my products need a bubble-lined mailer?
faqs.a: Look at how the failed items broke rather than at the packaging, and match the fix to the fracture. Impact damage suits a lining; crushing, abrasion and movement each need a different answer.

/canada/.h2: More questions about poly mailers for Canada

faqs.q: Are documentation and charges stated on Canadian poly mailer quotations?
faqs.a: Yes. For a Canadian order, documentation and any charges are stated on the quotation before you commit, rather than arriving as a surprise with the shipment. Quotations for Canadian customers are issued in Canadian dollars.

faqs.q: Can you advise on Quebec language rules for poly mailer artwork?
faqs.a: We are packaging manufacturers rather than legal advisers. Language legislation affects packaging sold in Quebec, so businesses there plan artwork around it rather than translating afterwards. What your business must do is a question for a qualified adviser.

faqs.q: Do Canadian poly mailers shipped into the US need a different specification?
faqs.a: A cross-border parcel from Canada faces more custody changes, documentation that must stay attached, and possible inspection. Our Toronto cross-border shipping guide explains what that means for the mailer specification.

faqs.q: Which Canadian cities are covered in your poly mailer guides?
faqs.a: Separate guides cover Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, Ottawa and Montreal, each on a different situation: cold-weather adhesive performance, plastics regulation, cross-border shipping, transit across a very large country, and French-language packaging.

faqs.a: Yes. On regulatory and language questions in Canada, our contribution is documentation and accurate material information rather than advice, which is more useful to whoever advises your business than a reassuring answer would be.

/christmas-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about Christmas poly mailers

faqs.q: How should Christmas poly mailer quantities be split?
faqs.a: Order themed Christmas mailers against a realistic forecast of gift-heavy parcels, and keep standard stock covering the rest of your volume throughout. A shortfall in themed packaging then slows nothing down, and the quantity at risk stays small.

faqs.q: Why do Christmas mailers need a designed label panel?
faqs.a: At peak volume, a label that lands on artwork every tenth parcel becomes a real scanning problem. Designing a clear white panel into the Christmas artwork gives packers an obvious place for the label every time.

faqs.q: How can Christmas mailers prevent seal failures at peak?
faqs.a: Seal failures rise when packing speeds up and temporary staff join. A deeper flap and a written sealing procedure both help Christmas parcels close properly, even on a hurried bench in December.

faqs.q: Why add a double adhesive strip to Christmas poly mailers?
faqs.a: Gift returns arrive in January, after the season. A second adhesive strip specified on December's Christmas mailers lets customers reuse the same bag, saving a consumable and a packing step during returns.

faqs.q: Should Christmas mailer sizes be simplified for temporary staff?
faqs.a: Yes. Temporary staff pack more slowly and make more errors, so fewer sizes with clear rules cost less over the Christmas peak than a perfectly optimized range that nobody can apply under pressure.

/colored-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about colored poly mailers

faqs.q: What is the difference between stock and matched colored poly mailers?
faqs.a: Stock colors are tones already produced on the film, with lower cost and shorter setup; you select rather than specify. Matched colors are made against your reference, with higher setup and a proof round before production.

faqs.q: What does running several colored poly mailers really cost?
faqs.a: Adding a color to one order is often cheaper than expected, because setup is shared where size, film and artwork match. The real cost comes after production: separate storage lines, bench cartons and run-out dates for each color.

faqs.q: How many colors should a new colored poly mailer range start with?
faqs.a: Start with two. Two tones give visible variety and stay manageable at the bench, and a larger range is a decision you can make later from real data on which colors ran out first.

faqs.q: Can I order blue, green or purple poly mailers?
faqs.a: Yes. Colors without their own page, such as blue, green, purple, red or yellow, can be quoted as stock or matched tones. If you plan to print, the base color narrows the inks that will read on it.

faqs.q: Can colored film be used on bubble-lined poly mailers?
faqs.a: Yes. Colored film is not limited to plain mailers, and a color can carry across plain and cushioned formats, though matching between the two needs checking. See the poly bubble mailer options for the cushioned format.

/compostable-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about compostable poly mailers

faqs.q: What should I check before starting a compostable poly mailer program?
faqs.a: Find out what collection your customers can access, decide what you will tell them to do with the bag, ask the supplier what is documented, check what you may print, and test the material against your contents.

faqs.q: How should compostable poly mailers be stored?
faqs.a: Heat and humidity affect compostable-material films more than conventional polyethylene, so cool, dry and dark storage matters more. Materials designed to break down do not sit in storage indefinitely, so order to your usage rate.

faqs.q: Do compostable poly mailers seal and perform like standard ones?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Compostable films can behave differently in strength, seal performance and shelf life, so run a sample against your actual contents before switching a whole order flow across to compostable mailers.

faqs.q: What will you confirm about a compostable poly mailer film?
faqs.a: We confirm what the supplier of the specific film can evidence for your order: which standard, assessed by whom, for which conditions. We were not supplied documentation for either home or industrial composting, so we state neither.

faqs.q: What if my customers cannot reach composting for compostable mailers?
faqs.a: Then the material may deliver no benefit, and an instruction that leads nowhere is worse than none. Tell customers the honest alternative, or consider a route that does not depend on infrastructure, explained in our sustainable poly mailer options.

/custom-frosted-poly-bags/.h2: More questions about custom frosted poly bags

faqs.q: Should a custom frosted poly bag go inside a mailer?
faqs.a: That is the common apparel setup. The frosted bag keeps the garment presented and clean, while the mailer takes the label and the handling. If the bag needs an address label on it, you want a mailer rather than a frosted bag.

faqs.q: Does white ink print well on custom frosted poly bags?
faqs.a: It can look crisp or washed out depending on the garment inside, because frosted film is translucent. Dark inks hold their edge whatever is behind them, so white ink is a risk on frosted bags whose contents vary.

faqs.q: Which print layouts suit custom frosted poly bags best?
faqs.a: Restrained ones: a mark, a row of care symbols, a size marker. Large solid areas reduce the translucency that is the reason for choosing a frosted bag, so a heavily printed design is better on opaque film.

faqs.q: Should custom frosted poly bags use a slider or press seal?
faqs.a: A slider is easier to operate one-handed, which suits customers reopening the bag. A press seal sits lower in a stack, which suits stockists shelving many frosted bags. Both are confirmed on your quotation.

faqs.q: Can custom frosted poly bags be made to my garment size?
faqs.a: Yes. Custom sizes for frosted bags are quoted against your folded garment measurements, so measure the piece as it will actually be folded and bagged rather than the garment laid flat.

faqs.q: Why do customers keep custom frosted poly bags after purchase?
faqs.a: A resealable frosted bag gets kept for travel or seasonal storage, which extends how long a brand mark stays in the customer's home. It is designed to be kept rather than torn open and thrown away.

/custom-order-policy/.h2: More questions about the custom order policy

faqs.q: Under the custom order policy, when can a specification still change?
faqs.a: Before the quotation is confirmed, anything can change: size, film, color, coverage and quantity. After confirmation but before the proof, specification changes are still possible, and the quotation is reissued so what is agreed stays unambiguous.

faqs.q: What does the custom order policy cover if mailers do not match the proof?

faqs.q: Is a manufacturing defect covered by the custom order policy?

faqs.q: Who is responsible under the custom order policy if a size does not fit?

faqs.q: What should I send when reporting a problem under the custom order policy?
