faqs.q: Does the custom order policy cover damage in transit?
faqs.a: Where we arranged the shipping, damage in transit is ours to resolve. Report it promptly with photographs of the packaging as it arrived, and we will confirm next steps in writing so both sides keep a record.

/custom-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about custom poly mailers

faqs.q: What order should custom poly mailer decisions be made in?
faqs.a: Settle the size on a sample, choose the base color and finish, decide coverage and sides, prepare artwork to specification, then approve a proof before production. Doing these out of order is what causes a second proof round.

faqs.q: What changes the price of custom poly mailers the most?
faqs.a: Quantity is the biggest lever, because setup is a fixed cost spread across the run. Coverage moves cost more than color count does, and a second side, matched brand colors and interior printing each add to the price.

faqs.q: Is interior printing available on custom poly mailers?
faqs.a: Yes. Printing inside the bag is a separate operation, quoted separately from exterior print, and it changes both cost and lead time. It creates a strong unboxing moment for the customer and is priced accordingly.

faqs.q: When is printing the reverse of custom poly mailers worth it?
faqs.a: A second side adds a production stage. It is worth it when the reverse carries returns or disposal information that customers read at the door, and less so when it is purely decorative.

faqs.q: Can I preview custom poly mailers before requesting a quote?
faqs.a: Yes. Our poly mailer design tool lets you choose size, color and finish and position your logo. It is an approximate guide, and final artwork is confirmed on a proof you approve before anything runs.

/custom-printed-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about custom printed poly mailers

faqs.q: Why choose the format before designing custom printed poly mailers?
faqs.a: Artwork is laid out for a surface. A design that reads well on flat film loses its edges on a cushioned surface and its contrast on a translucent one, so choosing the format first means briefing a designer once rather than twice.

faqs.q: Which custom printed format takes photographic artwork?
faqs.a: Flat-film custom poly mailers take anything, including photographic artwork. Cushioned bubble mailers suit bold shapes only, and frosted bags suit dark inks and restrained layouts.

faqs.q: What artwork suits printed bubble mailers among the custom printed formats?
faqs.a: Bold shapes with no fine detail. The cushioned surface of a personalized bubble mailer softens edges, so thin lines and small type that work on flat film can blur. Keep the mark simple and generously sized.

faqs.q: Why do repeat patterns suit custom printed poly mailers?
faqs.a: A repeat pattern, as on bee poly mailers, has no wrong place on the bag, so it survives folding, sealing and labeling better than a placed logo, which can end up under a label or the flap.

faqs.q: Which constraints apply to every custom printed poly mailer format?
faqs.a: Four: the flap folds over and hides what is near the top, the label needs a clear zone, artwork that runs to the edge needs bleed, and the bag is seen packed rather than flat, so edge-to-edge designs distort.

faqs.q: Can you tell me which custom printed format suits my artwork?
faqs.a: Yes. Send what you have and say which format you are considering, and we will tell you honestly what will survive and what needs changing. A recommendation costs nothing, and the quotation follows.

faqs.q: How do I test custom printed artwork against a weak element?
faqs.a: Take the most delicate element in your identity, such as a thin script or a pale tone, and check how it behaves on each format you are considering. Read our artwork file guidelines before briefing a designer.

/design-your-poly-mailer/.h2: More questions about the poly mailer design tool

faqs.q: Should I choose my size before using the poly mailer design tool?
faqs.a: Yes. The design tool is quickest when you already know the size, and a preview cannot tell you whether your product fits. Settle the size with a physical sample packed with a real order first.

faqs.q: Does the poly mailer design tool produce print-ready artwork?
faqs.a: No. The preview is a visual guide, not manufacturing artwork. Print-ready files are prepared to the artwork guidelines and confirmed on a proof that you approve before anything is printed.

faqs.q: Does the poly mailer design tool calculate a price?
faqs.a: No. Quantity, market and specification interact, so a price comes back from a person rather than a calculator that would be wrong. Your configuration is attached to the quote request so we price exactly what you built.

faqs.q: How large should my logo be in the poly mailer design tool?
faqs.a: Add artwork at a generous size. Marks read smaller on a packed, folded and labeled bag than they do on a flat preview, so a logo that looks large in the design tool is often about right in use.

faqs.q: Can I rely on colors shown in the poly mailer design tool?
faqs.a: Not for accurate color. A screen is backlit and film is not. Where a color matters commercially, ask for a physical check rather than approving from the design tool preview or a digital proof.

/economy-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about economy poly mailers

faqs.q: How do I work out whether economy poly mailers save money?
faqs.a: Divide the end-to-end cost of one failed parcel by the saving per economy mailer. The result is the failure rate at which the saving disappears, often a fraction of a percent. If failures rise more than that, it costs money.

faqs.q: Do economy poly mailers suit marketplace fulfillment orders?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Where the platform controls presentation, a plain economy bag is frequently the requirement rather than a compromise, especially for light, soft goods that put little stress on the film.

faqs.q: Are economy poly mailers suitable for internal stock transfers?
faqs.a: Yes. Stock movements between your own locations need containment rather than presentation, so an economy specification works well, as it does for low-value sample and literature sends.

faqs.q: When are economy poly mailers a false economy?
faqs.a: With anything that has a corner, high-value contents, high-return categories without a second strip, and brands whose customers photograph parcels. In each case the saving is smaller than the cost of failures or lost presentation.

faqs.q: Can I take only some of the economy poly mailer savings?
faqs.a: Yes. An economy specification is four separate decisions, covering film, branding, closure and stock quantity. You can take the savings that are safe for your operation and keep a stronger film where contents need it.

faqs.q: How should a bulk order of economy poly mailers be stored?
faqs.a: Bulk economy orders only pay off when volume is predictable and storage is dry and dark. Heat, humidity and sunlight age the adhesive strip, so a large stock kept in poor conditions can lose its closure quality.

/halloween-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about Halloween poly mailers

faqs.q: How do I size a Halloween poly mailer run correctly?
faqs.a: Work from parcels rather than price. Take last year's order volume across the Halloween campaign, or your closest estimate, and add a modest contingency. A volume discount on units you never use is not a saving.

faqs.q: Which colors keep Halloween mailers usable after October?
faqs.a: Rust, plum and warm neutrals read seasonal through November, while orange and black do not. An autumn palette extends the usable window of Halloween mailers into general autumn shipping.

faqs.q: Should Halloween mailer artwork include the year?
faqs.a: No. A year printed on the bag turns leftover Halloween mailers into waste. Without it, unused stock can run again the following season, which means you can order a little more freely.

faqs.q: Do pattern motifs work better than scenes on Halloween mailers?
faqs.a: Yes, for extending the window. A repeating pattern of pumpkins or bats reads as autumn, while a full haunted-house scene reads as one night. Motifs keep Halloween mailers useful for longer.

faqs.q: What if my Halloween poly mailers run out mid-campaign?
faqs.a: Plain stock finishes the campaign perfectly well. Customers notice a themed parcel, but they do not notice its absence over the last few days, so running out is far cheaper than over-ordering Halloween mailers.

faqs.q: Why should Halloween mailers still carry the brand mark?
faqs.a: Seasonal artwork that hides who sent the parcel wastes the recognition you have built. Keep the mark visible on Halloween mailers, and leave a clear label panel so dense artwork is not covered. See seasonal poly mailer planning.

/how-it-works/.h2: More questions about how poly mailer ordering works

faqs.q: What are the five stages of a poly mailer order?
faqs.a: Brief, specification, proof, production and dispatch. You tell us what you ship, we agree the specification in writing, you approve a proof, the run is produced and checked against it, then cartons are counted and shipped to your address.

faqs.q: At which points do poly mailer order changes stop being free?
faqs.a: The quotation and the proof are the two gates. Before them, change freely. After the quotation, specification changes mean a reissued quotation, and after proof approval, changes mean a new proof and possibly a new run.

faqs.q: What most often delays a poly mailer order?
faqs.a: Artwork approval: a design still being argued about, an approver who is unavailable, or licensed elements not yet cleared. A size change after artwork and a color approved from a screen are the next most common causes.

faqs.q: Who approves spelling and web addresses on a poly mailer proof?
faqs.a: You do. Proof approval includes spelling, your web address and your social handles. We have no way to know what those should say, and once approved they are what gets printed on the run.

faqs.q: How do I get an accurate first poly mailer quotation quickly?
faqs.a: Answer the eleven questions in the custom mailer ordering checklist before making contact. It takes about ten minutes, and it also gives you a brief to send several suppliers so their quotations are comparable.

/industries/.h2: Questions about the industries we supply

faqs.q: Which industries does The Poly Mailers write packaging guidance for?
faqs.a: Ten sectors: clothing and apparel, ecommerce, fashion boutiques, beauty and cosmetics, books and stationery, subscription businesses, accessories, small businesses, gift retail and electronics accessories. Each guide starts from the problems that sector actually faces.

faqs.q: Why are poly mailer guides written by industry rather than by product?
faqs.a: A list of bags does not help when the real question is how your category ships. An apparel operation solves for returns, a beauty brand for unmarked cartons, an electronics seller for hard corners. Same material, different problems.

faqs.q: What does each poly mailer industry guide include?
faqs.a: Each guide opens with what actually goes wrong in that category, then recommends five products with the reason each fits, and answers the questions buyers in that industry ask. Recommendations differ between industries even where products overlap.

faqs.q: Why are some industries not covered in the poly mailer guides?
faqs.a: Categories that mostly ship in cartons do not get a guide, because recommending a flexible bag for rigid goods would mean arguing against ourselves. We only cover sectors where poly mailers are genuinely the right packaging.

faqs.q: What if my industry is not among the poly mailer guides?
faqs.a: Describe what you ship, and we will tell you honestly whether a poly mailer suits it. If it does, we will recommend a specification and quote it; if your goods need a carton, we will say so.

faqs.q: What is the main poly mailer problem for clothing brands?
faqs.a: Sizing across a range that varies widely in bulk, and building returns into the packaging decision. Our clothing and apparel mailer guide covers the size mix and the double adhesive strip in detail.

faqs.q: What poly mailer issues do beauty and cosmetics brands face?
faqs.a: Protecting glass, pumps and printed retail cartons at the same time. A mailer that protects the product but lets the carton arrive scuffed has failed at something a beauty customer will notice immediately.

faqs.q: What damages books and stationery shipped in poly mailers?
faqs.a: Corners, creasing and moisture are the three things that damage paper in transit. A snug fit, a stiffener for thin items and a film outer address them, while a heavier film addresses none of them.

faqs.q: What makes electronics accessories different to ship in poly mailers?
faqs.a: Hard corners, moisture and a retail carton that has to arrive in sellable condition. Electronics accessory sellers also handle items where static is a concern, so the guide focuses on fit, cushioning and carton protection.

faqs.q: How should I brief you about my industry's poly mailer needs?
faqs.a: Send your order profile and the failures you are currently seeing, such as split seals or scuffed cartons. We will recommend a specification for your industry and explain the reasoning behind it, along with a written price.

faqs.q: How can an accessories range be covered with three mailer sizes?
faqs.a: Group by packed shape rather than product category. Small boxed items go in the smallest size, folded soft accessories in a mid size, and bags, totes and hats in a larger size. Outliers suit a plain oversized bag.

faqs.q: How do I stop buckles and clasps puncturing accessory mailers?
faqs.a: Buckles, clasps and studs behave like a corner pressing against the film from inside. Choose a heavier film weight or a lined mailer for accessories with hardware, so the concentrated force does not split the bag.

faqs.q: How do I stop chains and straps tangling in accessory parcels?
faqs.a: It is a packaging problem only in that a tight fit prevents movement. The real fix is how the accessory is presented inside, such as a card or pouch that holds the chain or strap in place.

faqs.q: Why is a small accessory in a large mailer a problem?
faqs.a: It is a common error when a business standardizes on one size. A small accessory in a large mailer moves, and movement is what causes damage, so keep a small size such as a 6x9 for jewelry and light boxed items.

faqs.q: Can mailer colors reduce picking errors for accessories sellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Accessories operations pick from a wide spread of product types, and color-coding mailers by product line is a cheap way to help a busy bench choose correctly. See our colored poly mailer range.

faqs.q: Should accessories gift orders have presentation inside or outside?
faqs.a: Decide whether you want to support gift-ready parcels. If yes, a colored bag with a seal sticker and tear tab covers it cheaply. If not, keep the accessory mailer practical and add gift presentation inside for orders that need it.

/industries/beauty-and-cosmetics/.h2: More questions from beauty and cosmetics brands

faqs.q: How do I stop cosmetic pumps and caps loosening in transit?
faqs.a: Vibration over a long journey loosens closures. The fix is tape or a seal on the cosmetic product itself rather than a change to the mailer, combined with a fit snug enough that the item cannot move.

faqs.q: How do I stop a leaking bottle ruining a beauty order?
faqs.a: Bag liquids individually inside the mailer. One leaking bottle ruins everything it touches, and individual bagging contains the damage to a single beauty product instead of the whole order.

faqs.q: Do beauty brands need fully printed mailers to look considered?
faqs.a: No. A matte film in a tone matching your secondary packaging, a seal sticker and a printed card inside read as considered without a full-coverage run. What reads badly is a scuffed parcel or product showing through a pale bag.

faqs.q: Which mailers suit beauty sample and gift-with-purchase sends?
faqs.a: Marketing sends are small, go out in bursts and carry low-value products. A small colored mailer with something printed inside usually outperforms a larger protective one for beauty samples, and costs less.

faqs.q: Should beauty glass bottles be boxed before going in a bubble mailer?
faqs.a: Yes. Bubble lining addresses glass breaking on impact, but boxing the item first addresses it better. Cushioning works across a face, so a carton gives the lining something even to protect.

faqs.q: Why do beauty cartons get crushed at the corners in mailers?
faqs.a: Corner damage on beauty cartons is mostly about fit rather than lining: a carton that cannot move cannot get crushed at the corner. Where crushing is the main risk, a rigid carton is the answer. Compare formats in our protective mailer guide.

/industries/books-and-stationery/.h2: More questions from books and stationery sellers

faqs.q: How do I pack flat stationery so it arrives flat?
faqs.a: Add a board stiffener cut to the mailer size, size the bag so nothing slides, face any printed side inward against the stiffener, seal onto clean film, and put the label on the flattest face of the parcel.

faqs.q: Does heavier film help protect books and stationery?
faqs.a: No. Corner damage, creasing and moisture are the three ways paper arrives damaged, and a heavier film addresses none of them. A snug fit, a stiffener and a film outer do far more for books and stationery.

faqs.q: Why do board-backed stationery parcels fail to seal properly?
faqs.a: Board reaching the adhesive strip is a common cause of partial seals in this category. Cut stiffeners slightly shorter than the mailer opening so the strip on a books or stationery parcel bonds to clean film.

faqs.q: Should art books and large prints use a 12x15 mailer?
faqs.a: A 12x15 suits larger prints, art books and multi-item stationery orders. Add a stiffener for anything thin, and choose a cushioned option if the corners of an art book must arrive unmarked.

faqs.q: Is a paper-faced padded mailer ever better for books?
faqs.a: It feels right for a book and takes fine print crisply, but a paper outer absorbs water. Paper contents in a wet paper bag is the worst combination, so if parcels sit on doorsteps in weather, film wins. See the poly versus padded mailer comparison.

faqs.q: What should a seller of thin prints and posters use instead?
faqs.a: A flat print needs a board stiffener in a close-fitting mailer, since flat items bend when a parcel is flexed. Where a print is too large for a board-backed mailer, roll it in a tube instead.

/industries/clothing-and-apparel/.h2: More questions from clothing and apparel brands

faqs.q: Why do clothing brands run two packaging flows, not one?
faqs.a: With fashion-level return rates, packaging serves an outbound and an inbound journey. A single-strip mailer works outbound but forces customers to find their own return packaging, adding a consumable and a worse return experience.

faqs.q: How do I calculate whether a double strip pays for clothing mailers?
faqs.a: Multiply the extra cost per mailer by your total volume, then compare it against your return rate multiplied by the cost of a returns bag plus the support contacts about how to send clothing back.

faqs.q: What clothing mailer sizes cover a typical apparel range?
faqs.a: Usually two or three: a standard size such as 10x13 for most single garments, a larger size for knitwear, denim and multi-item orders, and the largest for heavyweight hoodies and outerwear, which fail without it.

faqs.q: Why add frosted poly bags to clothing and apparel packaging?
faqs.a: A frosted bag is a presentation layer for garments going into retail or arriving as a gift. It keeps the piece clean and visible inside the mailer, which takes the label and the handling.

faqs.q: What mistakes do clothing brands make with mailer artwork?
faqs.a: The common one is a centered front design with no label plan, which gets covered on a large share of parcels. Design a clear label zone in, or move the artwork to the reverse and keep the clothing mailer front plain.

faqs.q: Which closure suits apparel mailers for clothing returns?
faqs.a: A double adhesive strip, as on self-seal poly mailers. The customer repacks the garment in the same bag, reseals it and sends it back, turning a clothing return into one bag instead of two.

faqs.q: Which packaging costs do ecommerce quotations not show?
faqs.a: Packer decision time, reorder admin, the share of parcels crossing a shipping threshold, damage rates and support contacts about returns. All are shaped by an ecommerce mailer specification chosen months earlier, and none appears on a quotation.

faqs.q: How should an ecommerce business review its mailer setup?
faqs.a: Pull a full month's order profile, map it to sizes, weigh packed samples against your rate card, check damage data by product type, write the bench rules down, and order the sizes on one run. Review annually against real data.

faqs.q: When should an ecommerce operation stop using one mailer size?
faqs.a: When roughly a fifth or more of parcels are either lost inside the standard size or straining it. At that point the wasted film and the damage together cost an ecommerce operation more than adding a second size would.

faqs.q: Why weigh packed ecommerce parcels against a carrier rate card?
faqs.a: That is where the real money is. A size change that moves ecommerce parcels across a carrier pricing threshold outweighs any unit-price saving on the mailer itself, in either direction.

faqs.q: Can consolidating ecommerce orders into one parcel cut costs?
faqs.a: It can. Multi-item ecommerce orders packed into a single 19x24 poly mailer travel as one parcel rather than several, but weigh a packed sample first, because a consolidated parcel can cross a threshold that two smaller ones stayed below.

faqs.q: Do self-seal mailers save time at ecommerce volume?
faqs.a: Yes. A self-seal closure saves seconds per parcel at the bench, and at ecommerce volume those seconds multiply across thousands of orders a month. A second strip also lets customers reuse the original bag for returns.

/industries/electronics-accessories/.h2: More questions from electronics accessories sellers

faqs.q: Are standard poly mailers anti-static for electronics components?
faqs.a: No. Standard polyethylene is not an anti-static material. If your electronics accessories include static-sensitive components that need anti-static handling, say so at the inquiry stage, because it changes the specification.

faqs.q: Why does moisture matter more for electronics accessories mailers?
faqs.a: Electronics and water are a total loss rather than a cosmetic problem. A film outer is not optional for electronics accessories in the way it can be for soft goods, so a paper-faced mailer is a poor choice here.

faqs.q: How should electronics accessory mailers be sized to protect cartons?
faqs.a: Size to the retail carton rather than the product. A carton that cannot move inside the bag cannot catch, rub or take a corner impact at speed, which is the most effective single change for electronics sellers.

faqs.q: Which mailer suits cables and adapters for electronics sellers?
faqs.a: A 6x9 poly mailer handles cables, adapters and small boxed electronics accessories. Larger cases, keyboards and multi-item orders suit a 9x12, with a cushioned option if a retail box must arrive unmarked.

faqs.q: When is a mailer not enough for electronics accessories?
faqs.a: Flexible packaging has no structure, so anything that must not be compressed cannot be protected by it whatever the lining. If your damage reports show crushing, electronics items need a rigid carton instead.

faqs.q: How do I reduce doorstep theft risk for electronics parcels?
faqs.a: Use opaque film and print nothing on the outside that names the product. Higher-value electronics in a bag that announces its contents is a theft risk, which is why black poly mailers suit this category.

faqs.q: Where should a fashion boutique spend a small packaging budget?
faqs.a: On a colored film, a printed seal sticker and something printed inside the bag. Together they give a boutique most of the presentation of a printed run at a fraction of the cost. Print the outer bag when volume makes it sensible.

faqs.q: Why does arrival condition matter more for boutique garments?
faqs.a: A boutique often cannot replace a damaged piece from stock, because it may be the only one. Fit, film and a clean seal therefore matter more for a fashion boutique than for a volume operation.

faqs.q: Which mailer finish photographs best for a fashion boutique?
faqs.a: Matte finishes and colored film photograph without hotspots, while gloss white does not. Independent fashion lives on customer content, so how a boutique parcel looks on camera is part of its job.

faqs.q: Should a fashion boutique add a returns strip to mailers?
faqs.a: Yes. Sizing returns are unavoidable in fashion, and a double adhesive strip costs very little while saving the exchange from feeling awkward. The customer simply reseals the boutique's original bag.

faqs.q: How many mailer sizes should a fashion boutique start with?
faqs.a: One: your most common order, which for many boutiques is a 10x13. Cover the outliers with a plain larger bag rather than a second branded line, so stock stays simple at low volume.

faqs.q: Can frosted bags lift a fashion boutique's presentation cheaply?
faqs.a: Yes. A custom frosted garment bag inside the mailer is a presentation layer that costs less than printing the outer bag, keeping the boutique piece clean and visible when the parcel opens.

/industries/gift-retail/.h2: More questions from gift retail sellers

faqs.q: Why should gift retail mailers avoid naming the product?
faqs.a: A product name printed across the front removes the surprise before the parcel is opened. Gift retail parcels often go straight to a recipient, so the outer bag should look intentional without giving the contents away.

faqs.q: How do gift retailers stop parcels looking like returns?
faqs.a: A plain gray bag with a large courier label reads as a returns shipment rather than a present. A colored mailer, a neat seal and a considered label position make a gift retail parcel read as a gift.

faqs.q: How should gift orders be flagged for the packing bench?
faqs.a: Flag gift orders at checkout, then use a different mailer color for them. The bench cannot pack a gift differently without knowing which orders are gifts, and color-coding makes the instruction visible.

faqs.q: Where should a personal message go in gift retail parcels?
faqs.a: Inside, on a card. A card is where personalization belongs in gift retail: it costs little, it is what the recipient keeps, and it avoids printing anything personal on the outer mailer.

faqs.q: How should gift retailers plan packaging for a seasonal peak?
faqs.a: A large share of gift volume arrives in a few weeks, ordered against a forecast made months earlier. Run themed stock alongside standard stock so a wrong forecast is cheap. See our Christmas poly mailer planning.

faqs.q: Can gift retail mailers carry cushioning and a printed message?
faqs.a: Yes. Personalized bubble mailers combine cushioning with printed branding on the same parcel, which suits gift retail items that need protection but should still look like a present on arrival.

faqs.q: Why should a small business avoid four mailer sizes at first?
faqs.a: Start with one size and add a second only when a real pattern of orders shows you need it. Each extra size is another line to store and reorder, which a small business shipping tens of parcels can do without.

faqs.q: Is a custom color match worth it for a small business?
faqs.a: Usually not yet. A stock color close to your brand costs far less and looks the same to a customer who has never seen your swatch. Custom matching makes sense for a small business once volume grows.

faqs.q: How can a small business look considered on its first parcels?
faqs.a: Customers register color, cleanliness and care first. A colored bag sealed neatly, with the label placed the same way every time, reads better for a small business than an elaborate print sealed carelessly.

faqs.q: Do patterned mailers suit a small business without bespoke artwork?
faqs.a: Yes. A stock pattern such as our bee poly mailers looks designed without a bespoke run, giving a small business a distinctive parcel before committing to its own artwork.

faqs.q: Should a small business with tiny products start with small mailers?
faqs.a: Yes. If your products are genuinely small, start with a small poly mailer size rather than 10x13. A small item in a large bag moves around, which causes damage and wastes film on every parcel.

faqs.q: How should a small business store packaging in limited space?
faqs.a: Keep cartons flat, dry and out of direct sun, and order a quantity you will use in a season. Heat and humidity age adhesive strips, and cash tied up in a small business's packaging is cash not in stock.

faqs.q: How do subscription businesses keep the twelfth parcel feeling special?
faqs.a: Through consistency of care rather than novelty: the same color, fold, label position and clean seal every month. A subscription mailer that arrives identical each cycle reads as a brand with standards.

faqs.q: How should subscription businesses size their mailer?
faqs.a: Fix the contents envelope first: decide the maximum bulk a monthly box can contain, then size the mailer to that rather than to an average month, so every subscription parcel closes cleanly.

faqs.q: How much spare packaging should a subscription business order?
faqs.a: Order against the subscriber count plus a small allowance for growth and reships, not plus a quarter of a year. A known count is the main packaging advantage subscription businesses have over other models.

faqs.q: Where should subscription businesses add monthly variety?
faqs.a: Keep the outer mailer constant and vary the inner layer: a card, tissue or seasonal insert. Those change cheaply each month without touching the subscription packaging specification.

faqs.q: Why should subscription businesses write down the packing standard?
faqs.a: A written standard covering fold, order of items, insert position and label placement is what makes month twelve look like month one, even when different staff pack the subscription boxes.

faqs.q: Are printed mailers economical for subscription businesses?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Printed runs get cheaper with quantity and need predictable volume to justify, and subscription supplies both. Our custom printed poly mailers can be quoted against your subscriber count.

/large-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about large poly mailers

faqs.q: Why do large poly mailers behave differently from small ones?
faqs.a: A small mailer is held rigid by its contents; a large one is not. Slack air, an uneven load or a hard corner in a large poly mailer all turn into movement, and movement is what opens seals and tears corners.

faqs.q: Is ordering one large mailer size bigger a safe choice?
faqs.a: No. Slack air makes a parcel less stable, not more forgiving. An over-large poly mailer damages more often than a correctly sized one and costs more per unit, so order the smaller size that closes without strain.

faqs.q: Why do seals fail when moving up to large poly mailers?
faqs.a: Sizing up usually means the contents got heavier too. Carrying the same light film weight into a bigger format is where most large mailer seal failures come from, so review film weight whenever you move up.

faqs.q: When is a large poly mailer not the right fix?
faqs.a: When contents arrive damaged rather than in a burst bag. More room will not fix impact damage; cushioning will. The protective mailer comparison guide is the better starting point if damage rather than fit is the problem.

faqs.q: Can I split a first order across two large mailer sizes?
faqs.a: Yes. If you are unsure after testing samples, splitting the first large poly mailer order between two candidate sizes lets real orders show which one suits your packing, before you commit fully to either.

faqs.q: Does consolidating parcels into large poly mailers lower shipping cost?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Consolidating four parcels into one large mailer can save money, or it can cross a pricing threshold and cost more. A bigger bag also holds fewer per carton, so weigh a packed sample before switching.

/light-pink-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about light pink poly mailers

faqs.q: Which ink reads most dependably on light pink poly mailers?
faqs.a: Black is the dependable choice that most blush ranges use. Warmer dark tones read as more considered at large sizes, while pale or tonal inks work only for large marks and lose small type on a light pink base.

faqs.q: Should opacity be chosen before the tone of a light pink mailer?
faqs.a: Yes. The opacity choice affects how the tone itself reads: the same blush on a denser film sits slightly cooler and flatter. Decide opacity first, then confirm the light pink tone on that film.

faqs.q: Is a light pink mailer right for a white wordmark brand?
faqs.a: No. White has too little separation from a blush base to hold an edge. If your identity is built on a white wordmark, a saturated tone will serve you better than light pink poly mailers.

faqs.q: Do light pink mailers need higher opacity for pale products?
faqs.a: Usually not. If most of what you ship is pale, such as cosmetics in white cartons, stationery or light garments, standard opacity is usually fine on light pink mailers and there is no reason to pay for more.

faqs.q: Why do light pink mailers suit fine jewelry brands?
faqs.a: A quiet blush outer parcel keeps attention on the jewelry box inside rather than competing with it. Light pink also sits well with beauty cartons, uncoated stationery papers and boutique fashion at higher price points.

faqs.q: Why do light pink mailers look different in customer photos?
faqs.a: Pale tones pick up the color of the surface they are photographed on, so a blush mailer can look peach on wood and mauve on gray. A matte finish reads more evenly, as our guide to choosing mailer colors explains.

/locations/.h2: Questions about the locations we serve

faqs.q: Which countries do The Poly Mailers location guides cover?
faqs.a: The United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia. Each market has a set of regional guides beneath it, and orders in all four are produced to your specification and shipped to your address.

faqs.q: Do the location guides mean you have local premises there?
faqs.a: No. We hold no branch, depot or collection point in any market. The location guides exist because each region raises a different commercial problem, not because we have a presence in those places.

faqs.q: Can any poly mailer insulate contents in an Arizona summer?
faqs.a: No. A poly mailer is not an insulated container, and no film weight or lining makes it one. A parcel in a hot Arizona van or on a doorstep reaches ambient temperature; packaging only affects how quickly.

faqs.q: Why ship earlier in the week during Arizona summers?
faqs.a: A parcel that sits over a weekend in a facility or vehicle has the longest heat exposure of any in the network. Shipping earlier in the week cuts that exposure for Arizona deliveries without changing the mailer at all.

faqs.q: Do white poly mailers help with Arizona heat?
faqs.a: A little. A white or light film in direct sun absorbs measurably less radiant heat than a black one, which matters for an Arizona parcel left on a doorstep. It slows warming but does not prevent it.

faqs.q: Do bubble-lined mailers help heat-sensitive Arizona shipments?
faqs.a: Marginally. A cushioned lining slows the rate at which contents reach ambient temperature, giving a small buffer. For genuinely heat-sensitive products in Arizona, insulated packaging or seasonal shipping limits are the real answer.

faqs.q: How should Arizona businesses store poly mailers through summer?
faqs.a: Closure adhesive degrades faster at high temperature. Order to a rate you will use, keep cartons sealed and away from external walls, and test a bag from any Arizona stock that has been sitting through the summer.

faqs.q: Which Arizona products are most affected by heat in transit?
faqs.a: Anything with a melting point: cosmetics, confectionery, adhesives and some plastics. Beauty and personal care is the most affected Arizona category, while soft goods and outdoor products designed for heat are largely unaffected.

faqs.q: Why does closure choice matter for Arizona poly mailers?
faqs.a: Heat affects adhesive, so the closure specification deserves extra attention for Arizona shipping. Our self-seal poly mailer options cover strip choices, and stock should be stored cool and used in rotation.

faqs.q: Why does packaging weight matter more for Atlanta air shipments?
faqs.a: A substantial share of parcels leaving Atlanta go by air at some point, and air shipping bills weight and volume more aggressively than road. Packaging weight becomes a direct, visible cost on Atlanta invoices.

faqs.q: What is the biggest billed-weight saving for Atlanta shippers?
faqs.a: Right-sizing the parcel. Under dimensional billing the air inside an oversized bag is charged whether or not anything is in it, so shipping less air is the biggest lever for Atlanta parcels by a wide margin.

faqs.q: Should Atlanta businesses swap cartons for poly mailers?
faqs.a: Where the contents allow it. A carton with void fill weighs several times what a mailer does and takes far more volume, so Atlanta shippers sending soft goods by air often save heavily by switching.

faqs.q: Do inserts add to billed weight on Atlanta parcels?
faqs.a: Yes. Every insert, filler and second bag is billed. Removing one component from every Atlanta parcel compounds quickly across a month of air shipments, often saving more than a lighter film would.

faqs.q: When does a lighter film stop saving Atlanta shippers money?
faqs.a: When the damage rate rises faster than shipping cost falls, which happens sooner than expected and immediately for hard corners or real weight. The economy poly mailer arithmetic shows where that point sits for your Atlanta operation.

faqs.q: Is a padded mailer lighter than a carton for Atlanta air freight?
faqs.a: Where cushioning is genuinely needed, a padded mailer is far lighter than a carton with void fill, which matters for Atlanta parcels billed by weight and volume on air legs.

faqs.q: What should an Atlanta business send to find packaging savings?
faqs.a: Send a packed parcel's weight and dimensions. We will tell you where the saving actually is for your Atlanta shipments, and it is usually in the parcel size or components rather than the bag itself.

faqs.q: Why do Austin creators rarely need printed mailers at first?
faqs.a: A creator's audience already knows who they bought from, so the parcel does not need to introduce the brand. An Austin creator needs confirmation instead: a color, a sticker, a handwritten line, or a card that sounds like them.

faqs.q: How should Austin creators handle unpredictable merch launches?
faqs.a: Keep a standing stock of plain bags so a launch never waits on a packaging order, and make the release-specific layer disposable: stickers and cards printed in small runs and changed every time.

faqs.q: Should Austin merch mailers carry a release name or date?
faqs.a: No. A date or release name on the bag turns leftover stock into waste for no benefit. Keep Austin merch mailers generic and put release-specific details on stickers or cards instead.

faqs.q: Which mailer colors suit Austin music and merch releases?

faqs.q: How should Austin creators forecast packaging quantities?
faqs.a: Order to the audience, not to hope. An Austin creator knows roughly how many followers are likely to buy, which is a better forecast than most retailers have, so order close to that number.

faqs.q: When does a printed mailer make sense for an Austin creator?
faqs.a: When merchandise stops being an occasional launch and becomes an ongoing operation. Predictable volume makes a printed run economical, and at that point a printed bag costs an Austin creator less per parcel than the sticker it replaces.

faqs.q: Which mailer size suits most Austin creator merchandise?
faqs.a: Merchandise is mostly apparel, so a 10x13 is the size most Austin creators need. Tech startups sending company merchandise and welcome packs often use the same size for event giveaways.

faqs.q: What do Birmingham trade customers need from a parcel?
faqs.a: Identification without opening, an accurate count, goods that arrive usable, and discretion where value is high. None of these is a logo, because a Birmingham trade parcel is checked against an order rather than enjoyed.

faqs.q: Why does B2B packaging failure cost Birmingham firms more?

faqs.q: Should Birmingham trade parcels be numbered and marked?

faqs.q: When is a mailer the wrong packaging for Birmingham trade goods?

faqs.q: Which mailers suit Birmingham jewelry and small valuable goods?

faqs.q: Which mailer specification suits Birmingham B2B component supply?

faqs.q: Why should Boston businesses order mailers more often in smaller quantities?

faqs.q: Do smaller mailer sizes make Boston deliveries easier?

faqs.q: Where should Boston businesses store poly mailers once delivered?

faqs.q: Why do blank mailers suit Boston businesses with limited space?

faqs.q: How should Brisbane businesses plan a summer peak for packaging?

faqs.q: Why do northern supplier calendars cause Brisbane ordering problems?

faqs.q: Why should Brisbane seasonal mailer quantities stay tight?

faqs.q: Do Brisbane fashion and swimwear brands face a different calendar?

faqs.q: How should Brisbane businesses store mailers through a warm peak?

faqs.q: Is a color per campaign cheaper for Brisbane businesses?

faqs.q: Why keep blank mailers alongside Brisbane Christmas stock?

faqs.q: Why do Calgary parcels seal at the bench but arrive open?
faqs.a: Cold reduces how readily pressure-sensitive adhesive flows into contact with the film, so a seal made cold is weaker. Calgary parcels then arrive open with an intact-looking strip, because the bond was partial from the start.

faqs.q: How should Calgary packers warm mailer stock in winter?

faqs.q: How should Calgary staff seal poly mailers in cold weather?
faqs.a: Give the strip a longer, firmer press than you would in summer. Cold adhesive needs more pressure and more time to form the same bond, and this costs Calgary packers nothing but a few seconds.

faqs.q: Why avoid tight-fitting mailers in a Calgary winter?
faqs.a: Cold film stretches less before it splits, so a parcel that was fine in July can fail in January at the same size. Calgary shippers often move up to a roomier size such as 12x15 in the cold months.

faqs.q: Is a seasonal heavier film worth it for Calgary shipping?

faqs.q: Which closure suits Calgary poly mailers in deep cold?

faqs.q: Should Columbus sample mailers carry any brand identification outside?

faqs.q: Do frosted bags help Columbus teams presenting pre-production samples?

faqs.q: What size mailer lets Columbus garment samples travel flat?

faqs.q: Are padded mailers sensible for Columbus samples that must arrive unmarked?

faqs.q: Can Columbus brands order sample mailers alongside their production mailers?

/locations/dallas/.h2: More questions about Dallas wholesale mailers
