faqs.a: Seasonal options include Halloween and Christmas poly mailers, along with bee poly mailers, a patterned design that works all year. The main risk with seasonal formats is quantity, so size the run to the window rather than carrying stock past it.

faqs.q: Does the poly mailer range include a budget specification for high volume?
faqs.a: Yes. Economy poly mailers are a cost-led specification for high-volume shipping, with an honest account of what the saving costs. Test that the film handles your contents, because a failed parcel quickly costs more than the unit saving.

faqs.q: Can I mix several products from the poly mailer range on one quote?
faqs.a: Yes. Many orders combine sizes, colors or constructions, and each is confirmed in writing before scheduling, so tell us what you ship and we will recommend what fits. Start with the poly mailer size comparison if size is the open question.

/printing-options/.h2: More questions about poly mailer printing options

faqs.q: What is the biggest lever for reducing poly mailer printing costs?
faqs.a: Quantity, because setup cost spreads across the run. After that, coverage moves cost more than color count does, since ink area matters more than the number of colors. Work down those decisions before cutting colors from the design.

faqs.q: Is logo-only printing a good poly mailer printing option?
faqs.a: Often. A single mark placed deliberately is the cheapest print available, and on a colored base it frequently looks more considered than heavy coverage. It also leaves clear space for the shipping label without designing a special panel.

faqs.q: Why plan the label position before choosing poly mailer printing coverage?
faqs.a: Full coverage leaves nowhere clean for a shipping label unless you design a clear zone in. Deciding label position before artwork stops the label covering your design and helps it stick to plain film. It is the step most often skipped.

faqs.q: When is printing both sides worth it among poly mailer printing options?
faqs.a: When the reverse carries something useful, such as returns or disposal information, or when the parcel will be seen from both sides. If not, a single printed face keeps the cost down. Add a second side when it does a real job.

faqs.q: What does a digital proof show for poly mailer printing?
faqs.a: It shows placement, scale and the relationship between elements accurately, so you can check nothing falls on the flap or under the label. It shows color only approximately. For an exact brand color, ask for a physical check before approving.

faqs.q: Does the poly mailer surface change which printing options work?
faqs.a: Yes. The same file behaves differently on flat film, a cushioned surface and translucent frosted film, and fine lines and pale inks can fail on some of them. Check the surface before commissioning artwork, and follow the poly mailer artwork guidelines when preparing files.

/protective-mailers/.h2: More questions about choosing protective mailers

faqs.q: How do I tell which protective mailer my damaged items need?
faqs.a: Look at how the items failed. Cracked or broken means impact, so bubble helps, and scratched means abrasion, so foam helps. Crushed means load, which calls for a carton, while items that moved inside the bag need a better fit.

faqs.q: Why can protective mailers not stop crushing damage?
faqs.a: A mailer has no structure, so whatever load is placed on top goes straight through to the contents, and no lining changes that. If products arrive crushed rather than knocked, accept early that a rigid carton is the answer instead of trying more cushioning.

faqs.q: Does fit matter as much as cushioning in protective mailers?
faqs.a: Yes. Cushioning only protects where it sits between the contents and the outside, so a small item in a large padded mailer has protection on its faces and open space beside it. It reaches the end of that space at speed, which is why you should size close to the item.

faqs.q: Which protective mailer suits items that arrive water-marked?
faqs.a: Choose a film outer rather than paper. A poly bubble mailer combines a moisture-resistant film face with impact protection, while paper-faced constructions absorb water and pass it to the contents. Truly water-sensitive items still need their own inner protection.

faqs.q: Can protective mailers carry tamper evidence for high-value contents?
faqs.a: Yes. Self-seal closure options include tamper-evident constructions that show if a parcel has been opened, which suits high-value contents. Combine the right closure with a cushioned construction if the item also needs protection from impact.

faqs.q: Is there a printed version of the cushioned protective mailers?
faqs.a: Yes. Personalized bubble mailers give the same cushioned protection printed with your artwork. The textured surface changes how artwork prints, so bold shapes and larger type work best, and you approve a proof on the actual material before production.

faqs.q: What should I send to get a protective mailer recommendation?
faqs.a: Tell us what is arriving damaged and how it failed, ideally with photographs. We will recommend a construction, explain the reasoning and quote it. The protective mailer comparison table matches contents to construction.

/recycled-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about recycled poly mailers

faqs.q: What is the difference between post-consumer and post-industrial recycled poly mailers?
faqs.a: Post-consumer material is recovered after a household or business used and discarded it, which diverts waste. Post-industrial material is manufacturing offcuts recovered before reaching a customer, so the environmental argument is weaker. Ask which one you are getting.

faqs.q: Why are most recycled poly mailers made from blended film?
faqs.a: Recycled feedstock alone affects how film runs in production and how it performs, so it is usually combined with a proportion of virgin polymer. A useful claim names the feedstock type and proportion and can be traced to a supporting document.

faqs.q: Can recycled poly mailers be made in pale or exactly matched colors?
faqs.a: Recycled feedstock limits how pale or how precisely matched a film can be. If an exact or very light color matters, tell us at quotation stage, and we will confirm what the available recycled film can reach before you order.

faqs.q: Does recycled content in poly mailers stay the same on reorder?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, because content can move between batches with available feedstock. Ask whether the figure is guaranteed on repeat orders or quoted per run. We confirm what the film for each order supports, in writing, with the supplier's documentation.

faqs.q: What documents back up a recycled poly mailer claim?
faqs.a: Usually a supplier declaration, a mill certificate or a third-party certification, and you should ask to see it rather than being told it exists. We provide what the film supplier can evidence for your order before you commit. See the sustainable mailer terminology guide.

/request-a-quote/.h2: Questions about requesting a poly mailer quote

faqs.q: What information does a poly mailer quote request need?
faqs.a: Six fields is enough for a real answer. The most useful details are what goes in the parcel including inserts, roughly how many over what period, the market it ships to, and a photograph of what you currently use. Send what you have.

faqs.q: Can I request a poly mailer quote without knowing the size?
faqs.a: Yes. If you are unsure of the size or the film, say so in the message. Working that out is part of the quotation rather than something you must settle first, and we come back with a size recommendation and a written specification.

faqs.q: How will I receive my poly mailer quote?
faqs.a: We read your request and reply by email to the address you give us. The reply confirms the specification in writing, covering size, film, closure, color, coverage and quantity, along with a price and a schedule.

faqs.q: How long is a poly mailer quote valid?
faqs.a: Each quotation carries a stated validity period, so you can compare it properly against other options without guessing when the price might change. If you need longer to decide, mention it when you request the quote.

faqs.q: Does a poly mailer quote commit me to ordering?
faqs.a: No. A quotation carries no obligation either way. Nothing is scheduled until you approve the written specification, and for printed work nothing runs until you also approve a proof, so you can review everything before committing.

faqs.q: Should I attach artwork to a poly mailer quote request?
faqs.a: If you have artwork, attach it, because it lets us check the file and price the print accurately. If it is not ready, the quote can still go ahead on size, film and coverage, and the artwork follows before a proof is produced.

faqs.q: Can I request samples with a poly mailer quote?
faqs.a: Yes. Samples and pricing are handled in the same conversation. Mention the sizes you want to test in the message, along with what goes inside, and we will work out what is useful to send and quote alongside it.

faqs.q: Can I phone instead of sending a poly mailer quote request?
faqs.a: Yes. A phone call is faster when you are still deciding what to order, and anything agreed that way is written back to you before it goes near production. For detailed specifications or artwork, email leaves a clearer record.

faqs.q: Does a poly mailer quote include shipping costs?
faqs.a: Yes. Shipping cost is quoted rather than absorbed into the unit price, so you can see it. The delivery address, schedule, shipping arrangement and any documentation for your market are also confirmed in writing on the quotation.

faqs.q: How can I make my poly mailer quote accurate first time?
faqs.a: Settle the key decisions first, such as size, film, closure, color and coverage, and include real quantities and dates. The custom mailer ordering checklist covers the eleven decisions that make a quotation accurate.

/resources/.h2: Questions about the poly mailer reference guides

faqs.q: Which poly mailer reference guide should I read first?
faqs.a: If you have not decided what to order, start with the size reference, then the color and material guides. If you are ready to request prices, the ordering checklist covers the eleven decisions that make a quotation accurate first time.

faqs.q: Are the poly mailer reference guides useful with other suppliers?
faqs.a: Yes, deliberately. Several guides tell you what to ask any supplier, including us. The material guide explains how to compare film specifications, and the ordering checklist works as a brief you can send to several suppliers for comparable quotes.

faqs.q: How do the poly mailer reference guides differ from the blog articles?
faqs.a: The guides are reference material, tables and checklists you come back to while working out an order. The articles are arguments you read once. Each guide also says what it does not cover and which page does.

faqs.q: Why do the poly mailer reference guides contain no gauge figures or percentages?
faqs.a: Because we will not publish numbers we cannot stand behind for your order. Film gauge varies by market and run, recycled content varies by batch, and delivery time depends on the order, so each is confirmed in writing on your quotation instead.

faqs.q: Which poly mailer reference guide helps with first-time artwork?
faqs.a: The printing and artwork guide is a start-to-finish walkthrough for someone preparing packaging artwork for the first time, covering file formats, bleed, color mode and what to check before a proof. Read it before briefing a designer.

faqs.q: Which poly mailer reference guide covers measuring awkward products?
faqs.a: The mailer measurement guide covers the three measurements that matter and how to take them on an awkward product. Use it with the size reference to shortlist two candidate sizes, then confirm with samples before ordering volume.

faqs.q: Is there a poly mailer reference guide for ordering outside the US?
faqs.a: Yes. The international ordering guide sets out what actually differs between the four markets served, such as currency, documentation and delivery arrangements, and what to settle before placing an order into a market for the first time.

faqs.q: Which poly mailer reference guide explains environmental terms?
faqs.a: The sustainable mailer terminology guide explains what each term commits you to and gives five questions to put to anyone making an environmental claim. Read it before briefing a designer on any wording you plan to print on the bag.

faqs.q: Which poly mailer reference guide explains closures and seal failures?
faqs.a: The closure and self-seal guide explains how closures work, why they fail and which construction suits which operation, including double-strip returns closures and tamper evidence. It is useful when parcels arrive open or returns arrive in mixed packaging.

faqs.q: Can I skip the poly mailer reference guides and just ask for advice?
faqs.a: Yes. Describe what you ship and we will do the working out, with a size recommendation, a written specification and a price, and a partial brief still gets a useful reply. You can send a short quote request at any time.

/resources/closure-and-self-seal-guide/.h2: More questions from the closure and self-seal guide

faqs.q: How does a self-seal poly mailer adhesive strip actually bond?
faqs.a: The strip carries a pressure-sensitive adhesive that is already active under a release liner. Folding the flap places it near the film, but the bond forms in proportion to pressure, so pressing firmly along the whole strip is what makes it stick.

faqs.q: Why do self-seal poly mailer closures open from the corners?
faqs.a: Packers often press the middle of the strip and not the ends, and seals open from the corners first. Press along the full length, especially the ends, to stop a partial bond failing somewhere in a sorting hub.

faqs.q: Can torn release liners ruin a poly mailer self-seal closure?
faqs.a: Yes. A liner torn off in stages leaves paper fragments stuck to the adhesive, and those patches will not bond. Peel the liner in one smooth motion and check the strip is clean before folding the flap over.

faqs.q: Does bench cleanliness affect poly mailer self-seal performance?
faqs.a: More than people expect. Dust, moisture or hand cream on the adhesive weaken the bond. Keep the packing area clean and dry, and avoid touching the exposed adhesive, so the strip meets clean film along its whole length.

faqs.q: When should I choose a tamper-evident poly mailer closure?
faqs.a: When you need to prove whether a parcel was opened, such as for high-value contents or parcels left in shared spaces. A tamper-evident construction shows visible signs of opening, which a standard single-strip closure does not.

faqs.q: How do I test old poly mailer self-seal stock before using it?
faqs.a: Peel, seal and pull firmly on a few bags from the stock in question. If the bond lifts easily, the adhesive has aged, usually through heat, humidity or light. Use fresher stock for outbound orders and improve storage.

faqs.q: Is a double-strip poly mailer closure worth it for returns?
faqs.a: It depends on your return rate. A double strip with a tear line lets customers open, repack and reseal the original bag with no extra packaging. The arithmetic is set out on the self-seal poly mailer page.

/resources/color-selection-guide/.h2: More questions from the color selection guide

faqs.q: Which three questions narrow a poly mailer color selection quickly?
faqs.a: Ask whether color or print carries the identity, how dark your contents are, and whether customers will photograph the parcel. Answer those before looking at swatches, and the shortlist usually narrows to two colors.

faqs.q: Why do pale mailer colors look gray over dark products?
faqs.a: Pale film over dark contents lets them shadow through, which is the most common color complaint, especially on blush mailers. Specify opacity as well as tone, because opacity also changes how the color itself reads.

faqs.q: Does matte or gloss photograph better when selecting a mailer color?
faqs.a: Matte photographs evenly. Gloss produces hotspots that need lighting to control. If customers are likely to share unboxing photos, decide finish and tone together, since the same pigment can look like two different colors on each.

faqs.q: Can mailer color selection reduce picking errors on a packing bench?
faqs.a: Yes. Coding order types, product lines or markets by mailer color helps packers pick correctly at a busy bench without any printing. It is one of the few decisions that improves both accuracy and recognition at the same time.

faqs.q: How can stored mailer stock end up in mismatched colors?
faqs.a: Prolonged light exposure affects color on film, so a pallet stored by a window will not match one kept at the back. Store cartons sealed and out of sunlight, and use them in rotation so older stock does not drift visibly.

faqs.q: How does lighting change mailer color choices for retail brands?
faqs.a: A color chosen in good daylight can read as cheap under fluorescent strip lighting or look grubby after handling. Judge shortlisted colors in the light where they will be seen, and assess samples after handling rather than as clean swatches.

faqs.q: Should several mailer colors be ordered on one run?
faqs.a: Where several tones run together, ordering them on a single run keeps the batches matched and can share setup. That helps when colors code product lines. See how matching works on the colored poly mailers page.

/resources/custom-mailer-ordering-checkl.h2: More questions from the mailer ordering checklist

faqs.q: Which item on the custom mailer ordering checklist matters most?
faqs.a: The first one: what goes in the parcel. Almost every expensive mistake traces back to a size chosen from a chart rather than a packed sample, and size constrains everything downstream, from artwork panels to film weight and shipping bands.

faqs.q: Why does the mailer ordering checklist ask for a monthly rate?
faqs.a: A monthly rate tells a supplier how to structure the order, such as one run or several deliveries, while a single total does not. It also helps plan storage, because holding too much stock ages the closure adhesive.

faqs.q: What attachments speed up a custom mailer quote from the checklist?
faqs.a: A photograph of a packed parcel, your artwork even in rough form, a physical color reference and your delivery address with its type. Those four remove a round of correspondence and let a supplier flag problems early.

faqs.q: Why does the mailer ordering checklist ask for a delivery date?
faqs.a: A date, not a duration, is what everything else works backwards from, including proof approval and production. Give the date stock must be on the bench, and the schedule on your quotation can be built around it in writing.

faqs.q: How does the mailer ordering checklist handle closure choice?
faqs.a: It asks whether you need a single strip, a double strip for returns or a tear feature, which depends mainly on your return rate. If a meaningful share of orders come back, a double-strip closure often replaces a separate returns bag.

faqs.q: What should I check before comparing quotes from the mailer ordering checklist?
faqs.a: Check each describes the same thing: film weight, whether shipping is included, the same quantity and the same size measurement. Then prefer quotations that name the film, closure, quantity tolerance and proof process over a bare price.

faqs.q: Can I send the custom mailer ordering checklist to several suppliers?
faqs.a: Yes. Sending the same eleven answers to several suppliers gives you quotations you can actually put side by side. When you are ready, request a poly mailer quotation with the same answers.

/resources/international-ordering-guide/.h2: More questions from the international ordering guide

faqs.q: Why do fulfillment centers matter in international mailer ordering?
faqs.a: Fulfillment centers often have booking, labeling and palletization requirements that must be built into the order. Confirm the exact delivery address and its type first, because reaching a fulfillment center and a small business address are different logistics problems.

faqs.q: Can printed mailer wording differ between international markets?
faqs.a: Yes. Environmental and performance claims are governed differently in each market, so the same printed bag may not be compliant everywhere it ships. Review printed wording, especially environmental claims, against local rules before approving artwork.

faqs.q: Should international mailer orders start with a single market?
faqs.a: If you can. A first shipment into a new market teaches you things a quotation cannot, such as delivery quirks and paperwork. Learning them on a smaller order is cheaper than discovering them on a large multi-market run.

faqs.q: Which spelling should printed mailers use across international markets?
faqs.a: Decide deliberately. Spellings of common words such as color and personalized differ between US, UK, Canadian and Australian English, and so does the way sizes are expressed. Choose one convention for the printed bag rather than letting a designer pick by default.

faqs.q: When should one mailer specification be split for international markets?
faqs.a: A single specification usually wins when volumes are similar everywhere. Where one market dominates, it is often cheaper to optimize for that market and treat the others separately, especially if a film or color is unavailable in one of them.

faqs.q: When should material availability be checked in international mailer ordering?
faqs.a: Before you design anything. Not every film, finish, color or material is available for every market, and an unavailable option changes the specification. We check availability for your destination market before you order, not after.

/resources/mailer-measurement-guide/.h2: More questions from the mailer measurement guide

faqs.q: How should depth be measured in the mailer measurement method?
faqs.a: Under light pressure, the way a packer presses while sealing. Measuring an uncompressed lofty item overstates what you need, while squashing it flat understates it. Measure where a hand would realistically hold it.

faqs.q: How much closure allowance does the mailer measurement method need?
faqs.a: Enough that contents sit below the adhesive strip and the flap folds onto clean film. If contents reach the strip, that section will not bond. Test by packing and sealing a real order rather than relying on a fixed figure.

faqs.q: How do I measure irregular soft goods using the mailer measurement guide?
faqs.a: Measure the smallest rectangle the packed item fits inside, because that rectangle is what the bag must accommodate. For several items of different shapes, pack them together as they will ship and measure the bundle, not each item.

faqs.q: How should rigid boxes be measured for a poly mailer?
faqs.a: Rigid boxes are easy to measure and unforgiving in use. Size close, because a box that can move inside the bag will damage its own corners. Measure to the outer dimensions and leave only the room the closure needs.

faqs.q: How do protruding parts change measurements for a poly mailer?
faqs.a: Measure to the extremity of a handle, strap or spout, and consider whether it should be tucked or taped before packing. A protrusion that cannot be tucked may point toward a different format or a carton.

faqs.q: Why can two suppliers quoting the same mailer measurement differ?
faqs.a: Some quote the usable area with the flap above it, others the overall size including the flap, and some round to nominal figures. Two identical numbers can describe different bags, so ask which is quoted or compare physical samples.

faqs.q: Why weigh the parcel while taking mailer measurements?
faqs.a: Weight and depth together decide which shipping band a parcel falls into, and a size change can move it either way. Weigh the packed parcel while you have it. Match the measurements in the poly mailer size guide.

/resources/poly-mailer-material-guide/.h2: More questions from the poly mailer material guide

faqs.q: Why can two poly mailer films with equal stated thickness perform differently?
faqs.a: Thickness alone does not decide performance. How the film was produced, what it is blended from and how the seals were made all affect whether a bag survives a drop, so identical figures can still behave noticeably differently.

faqs.q: Is a poly mailer film thickness figure a target or a minimum?
faqs.a: Ask the supplier, because it matters. A minimum is a commitment, while a target is an aspiration, and the difference shows at the bottom of a run. Two quotes can look equal until you find one quoted a target and one a minimum.

faqs.q: How do I drop-test poly mailer film samples without equipment?
faqs.a: Pack both samples with your real heaviest order, then drop each once flat from bench height onto a hard floor and again on a corner. The corner drop is where concentrated force shows up and where weaker film fails.

faqs.q: How do I check poly mailer film water resistance at home?
faqs.a: Wet the outside and leave water on the panel and around the closure for a while, then check whether anything reached the contents. Film itself does not absorb water, so this mainly tests how well the closure and seal keep water out.

faqs.q: What does asking about the next poly mailer film weight tell me?
faqs.a: Knowing what an upgrade buys you shows where the current specification sits. A supplier who explains the next weight in terms of your contents, rather than just a number, is usually thinking about your actual problem.

faqs.q: How should poly mailer material claims about recycled content be checked?
faqs.a: Ask for the feedstock type, the proportion and a supporting document, all three. Without them the claim is decorative. Ask both suppliers the same question, and how each handles it tells you a lot about the rest of the quotation.

faqs.q: Can changing poly mailer film fix damage caused by poor fit?
faqs.a: No. Contents moving in an oversized bag, or a rigid item in a flexible one, will fail on any film weight. Confirm which failure you have before comparing materials, using the protective format comparison.

/resources/poly-mailer-size-guide/.h2: More questions from the poly mailer size reference

faqs.q: What does the poly mailer size reference assume about each order?
faqs.a: Each row assumes a single item packed with a card and a returns slip, folded competently. If you add tissue, a sticker sheet, a sample or a second item, move up a row. Size against the complete order you actually send.

faqs.q: Does the poly mailer size reference account for product protection?
faqs.a: No. Fitting and surviving are different questions, and the table tells you which size the item goes in, not whether it will arrive intact. If contents are fragile, the format, such as bubble lining or a carton, matters as much as the size.

faqs.q: Which size in the poly mailer size reference suits bedding sets?
faqs.a: Bedding and full double sets usually move into the consolidation size, the 19x24, while square soft goods such as cushions suit the 24x24. If the load exceeds a comfortable carry, consider whether one parcel or two works better on your rates.

faqs.q: When does a hardback book move up in the poly mailer size reference?
faqs.a: A paperback usually fits the single-garment size, but a hardback or oversized book moves up a row. Books need a close fit so corners cannot travel, so pack the actual title and check it seals onto clean film.

faqs.q: Why does fold quality change results in the poly mailer size reference?
faqs.a: A garment folded at speed takes more room than one folded carefully. The table assumes a competent fold, so size against the fold your packers actually produce at working pace rather than a neat demonstration.

faqs.q: What if my product is missing from the poly mailer size reference?
faqs.a: Measure a packed parcel rather than picking the nearest match, especially for lofty or irregular items. The mailer measurement guide covers packed depth as well as footprint.

faqs.q: Why compare bags rather than numbers in the poly mailer size reference?
faqs.a: Suppliers measure differently. Some quote to the flap and some to the usable area, so two bags with the same stated size can hold different amounts. Comparing physical samples removes that ambiguity in minutes.

/resources/printing-and-artwork-guide/.h2: More questions from the printing and artwork guide

faqs.q: Which areas should mailer artwork avoid according to the printing guide?
faqs.a: Draw the flap area and the side welds onto your template and keep anything important out of both. Also draw a clear zone for the shipping label, which is the most commonly skipped step, so the logo is never covered.

faqs.q: Why should mailer artwork use CMYK or spot colors rather than RGB?
faqs.a: An RGB file will be converted for print, and the conversion is where color surprises come from. Set color deliberately as CMYK or a named spot color from the start, so what you approve is closer to what prints.

faqs.q: Why outline fonts in poly mailer printing artwork files?
faqs.a: Live fonts can substitute silently when the file is opened elsewhere, changing your type without warning. Outlining the fonts removes that whole class of problem and keeps the lettering exactly as designed.

faqs.q: Which design choices survive packing according to the printing and artwork guide?
faqs.a: Fewer, larger elements, strong contrast, heavier line weights and a centered composition with breathing room. Edge-to-edge designs distort once something is in the bag, and subtle tonal palettes turn to mush on film under fluorescent light.

faqs.q: What should I personally check on a poly mailer artwork proof?
faqs.a: Check spelling, your web address, social handles and that the mark is the current version, since we cannot know those are wrong. Then check placement against a packed bag, including where the label lands and how the flap folds.

faqs.q: Does mailer artwork need changing for bubble or frosted surfaces?
faqs.a: Usually. A cushioned surface breaks up fine lines and closes small type, and frosted film reduces contrast because contents show through, so expect heavier weights and simpler shapes rather than a rescale. See the artwork file specification.

/resources/protective-mailer-comparison/.h2: More questions from the protective mailer comparison

faqs.q: What does the protective mailer comparison assume about fit?
faqs.a: It assumes the mailer is sized so contents cannot move. If they can move, fix that first, because it will change the answer. Movement causes inconsistent damage and rattling, and the fix is sizing down or filling the space.

faqs.q: Which construction does the protective mailer comparison suggest for scuffs?
faqs.a: Scratched or scuffed items point to abrasion, so foam lining or a tighter fit that stops rubbing is the answer. Adding bubble will not help, because bubble addresses impact rather than surface wear.

faqs.q: What does damage only at the corners mean in the protective mailer comparison?
faqs.a: Concentrated force. Cushioning works across a face, and a corner focuses a drop where the lining is thinnest. Box the item first, then cushion it, rather than relying on a thicker lining alone.

faqs.q: Can any mailer in the protective mailer comparison survive immersion?
faqs.a: No. A film outer resists rain and splashing, but it is not sealed and water enters at the closure. Anything that would be ruined by water needs its own sealed protection inside, whichever construction you choose.

faqs.q: Why does cushioning raise costs beyond unit price in the protective mailer comparison?
faqs.a: A cushioned mailer costs more, weighs more and makes a larger outer parcel for the same interior, which can move shipments into a higher pricing band. Weigh and measure a packed parcel against your rate card before switching.

faqs.q: Should I protect every product line after reading the protective mailer comparison?
faqs.a: Usually not. Damage tends to concentrate in one product type, and protecting only that line costs a fraction of protecting everything. Check returns and complaints by product before changing the whole flow.

faqs.q: Which items in the protective mailer comparison need only plain film?
faqs.a: Soft goods with nothing to protect against beyond weather, and hard-wearing items where moisture is the real risk, usually need only plain film. Compare cushioning options on the padded poly mailers page.

/resources/sustainable-mailer-terminolog.h2: More questions from the sustainable terminology guide

faqs.q: What does recycled content mean in the sustainable mailer terminology guide?
faqs.a: It is a statement about where the material came from, saying nothing about what happens after use. It needs a feedstock type, post-consumer, post-industrial or blended, and a proportion, both supported by a document.

faqs.q: Why does recyclable depend on customers in the sustainable terminology guide?
faqs.a: Recyclable means the material can be collected and reprocessed, which depends on infrastructure available to your customer, not the material alone. Flexible film is generally not accepted curbside in the markets served, so check where customers can take it.

faqs.q: What evidence does a compostable claim need under the sustainable terminology guide?
faqs.a: An assessment against a defined process plus a facility the customer can actually reach. Industrial and home composting are assessed differently, and a material may meet one and not the other, so the claim must say which.

faqs.q: Why is degradable not the same as biodegradable in the terminology guide?
faqs.a: Degradable or oxo-degradable means the material fragments, and fragmentation is not biodegradation. Additive-based fragmentation has drawn specific regulatory concern in several markets, which makes this wording risky to print.

faqs.q: Which claim does the sustainable terminology guide say you can evidence yourself?
faqs.a: A reduction claim based on before and after weights from your own operation, such as right-sizing or removing components. It needs nobody else's cooperation, which makes it a sensible first sustainability claim to make.

faqs.q: Do environmental claim rules differ between markets in the terminology guide?
faqs.a: Yes. The United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia each publish guidance on environmental claims, and it differs between them, so check any bag shipping to several markets against each. See the sustainability policy and claims position.

/samples/.h2: More questions about poly mailer samples

faqs.q: Why request two candidate sizes when ordering poly mailer samples?
faqs.a: The comparison is what produces the answer. A single sample tells you whether that size works, while two tell you which is right. Pack your heaviest routine order into each and choose the smaller one that closes without strain.

faqs.q: Should poly mailer samples include the next film weight up?
faqs.a: If the decision is finely balanced, yes. Weight differences are obvious in the hand and invisible on a specification sheet. Press a box corner or buckle against each film from inside, which is the most telling test between two weights.

faqs.q: Can poly mailer samples show my production color accurately?
faqs.a: Not reliably. A stock sample is not a proof of your specification, and color on film varies with finish, base and batch. Where color matters commercially, ask for a proof of your artwork on your chosen film rather than judging from a sample bag.

faqs.q: Why weigh packed poly mailer samples against shipping bands?
faqs.a: Weight and packed size decide which shipping band you land in, and this is where a size decision quietly saves or costs real money. Weigh and measure each packed sample against the bands you actually buy on before choosing.

faqs.q: Should I test a returns strip with poly mailer samples?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are weighing one. The only way to judge a double-strip closure is to use it: open along the tear line, repack the item and reseal. Mention the closure you would specify when requesting samples so the right construction is sent.

faqs.q: What can poly mailer samples not tell me about a full run?
faqs.a: A single bag is one data point, while a run has variation that production checks exist to control. Samples also cannot tell you what customers will think, which argues for a modest first order. Request samples with a quote in one message.

/seasonal-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about seasonal poly mailers

faqs.q: How many seasonal poly mailer campaigns should a brand plan each year?
faqs.a: Only the windows that genuinely move revenue, which for most businesses is one or two rather than six. A campaign that does not change sales does not need its own packaging, and fewer runs means less risk of stock left over.

faqs.q: Do seasonal poly mailers need to cover every parcel in a campaign?
faqs.a: Rarely. Gift orders and new customers are usually enough to carry the theme, with standard stock covering the rest. That lets you order the themed quantity tightly while a shortfall never slows orders down.

faqs.q: Which seasonal poly mailer designs can run again next year?
faqs.a: Undated artwork in a seasonal palette, rather than event-specific wording or a year, can be used the following season. Designs naming a specific date or event become dead stock as soon as the window closes, so decide this at design stage.

faqs.q: Why are Christmas poly mailers riskier to schedule than other seasonal runs?
faqs.a: Christmas is the highest-volume window and the one with capacity risk, so late orders compete with everyone else's peak. Fix the date stock must be on the bench and work backwards through proof approval and production, then confirm the schedule in writing.

faqs.q: How tightly should Halloween poly mailers be ordered?
faqs.a: Tightly. Halloween is a short window that closes hard, and leftover stock is difficult to use afterward. Run standard mailers underneath so a themed shortfall does not stop orders, and size the themed run to the parcels you expect in that window.

faqs.q: Are bee poly mailers an alternative to seasonal poly mailers?
faqs.a: For many small brands, yes. Bee poly mailers are patterned with no season attached, so leftovers are never dead stock. Brands running a genuine gift season justify a seasonal run, while those wanting a considered parcel year-round often do better with a pattern.

faqs.q: Can I see a printed seasonal poly mailer before ordering the full run?
faqs.a: Yes. Every printed run is proofed before production and nothing runs until you approve it, and you can ask about samples alongside your quote to check film and finish. See the poly mailer samples guide for what to request.

/self-seal-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about self-seal poly mailers

faqs.q: When is a tear tab worth adding to self-seal poly mailers?
faqs.a: When the opening is part of the experience, as on gift and subscription ranges, or when a returns strip must survive opening. A printed tear line shows the recipient where to open, so no scissors are needed and the second strip stays usable.

faqs.q: Why should labels go on after sealing self-seal poly mailers?
faqs.a: A label applied across the sealed flap lifts at the edges and can pull the seal open in transit. Seal first, then place the label on a flat area of the bag away from the closure, where it can be pressed down fully.

faqs.q: Does a deeper flap help self-seal poly mailers on full parcels?
faqs.a: Yes. A deeper flap gives the adhesive more film to meet, which helps on fuller parcels where contents sit close to the opening. It is a small specification change worth considering if your orders often fill the bag.

faqs.q: How do self-seal poly mailers speed up packing compared with tape?
faqs.a: A self-seal strip removes the tape dispenser from the bench, saving measurable seconds on every parcel at volume. There is no second consumable to buy, store or run out of. Plan for the release liner waste, which becomes its own stream on busy benches.

faqs.q: Do self-seal poly mailers help with missing-item disputes?
faqs.a: A tamper-evident construction gives you something factual to point at when a customer reports missing contents, because it shows visible evidence if the bag was opened. It suits high-value contents or a documented chain of custody. Read the closure and self-seal guide.

/shipping-and-delivery/.h2: More questions about mailer shipping and delivery

faqs.q: Why is no standard delivery time published for poly mailer orders?
faqs.a: Production depends on specification, quantity, printing and how quickly a proof is approved, and transit depends on destination, weight and service. One figure would be wrong for most orders, so we confirm a written schedule for yours at quotation.

faqs.q: Is shipping cost included in the poly mailer unit price?
faqs.a: No. Shipping cost is quoted separately rather than absorbed into the unit price, so you can see it. The quotation also states who bears the cost at each stage and how the order travels to your address.

faqs.q: What should I check when a poly mailer delivery arrives?
faqs.a: Check the carton count against the delivery note before signing. If an order arrives damaged or short, tell us promptly, and what happens next is set out in the custom order policy for made-to-order runs.

faqs.q: How should poly mailer cartons be stored after delivery?
faqs.a: Store cartons flat, sealed, off the floor and out of direct sunlight, and rotate so the oldest are used first. The film is stable, but the closure adhesive ages, and heat and light are what age it.

faqs.q: Do larger poly mailer orders arrive on pallets?
faqs.a: Larger orders arrive in cartons on a pallet. If your address has no loading dock, limited access or restricted parking, say so at quotation stage, and the delivery arrangement can be planned around those constraints rather than a standard pallet drop.

faqs.q: Should I mention a launch date when arranging poly mailer delivery?
faqs.a: Yes. A fixed date, such as a campaign launch, peak season or retail delivery window, changes what we recommend. We give you the date to work backwards from, including when proof approval becomes the critical path for your order.

/size-guide/.h2: More questions about the poly mailer sizing method

faqs.q: How many products should I test using the poly mailer size guide method?
faqs.a: Pick your five most-shipped products rather than the whole range. Five usually covers most of your order volume, and they tend to cluster into two or three sizes. Build a real order for each, including all inserts, and test from there.

faqs.q: Why drop-test parcels when following the poly mailer size guide?
faqs.a: Drop each packed parcel once from bench height, flat onto a hard floor. A seal that opens on one drop will open in a sorting hub. It is a quick way to catch a size that is too tight before you commit to a run.

faqs.q: Which measurement matters most in the poly mailer size guide?
faqs.a: Packed depth, the one most people skip. It decides both fit and which shipping band you land in. Flat product dimensions are almost useless on their own, because a flat garment tells you little about its folded size.

faqs.q: Can choosing too tight a size raise costs under the poly mailer size guide?
faqs.a: Yes. Forcing contents into a tight bag can make the parcel thicker, costing more in shipping than the film saved, and it can stop the strip meeting clean film. Weigh and measure the packed parcel against your rates before deciding.

faqs.q: Why does the poly mailer size guide warn against one size for everything?
faqs.a: A single size wastes film and shipping on light orders and fails on heavy ones. Two or three sizes chosen from real order data usually cover the range with clear boundaries, without asking packers to make constant decisions.

faqs.q: Should damaged parcels change the size chosen with the poly mailer size guide?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. If parcels arrive damaged rather than burst, sizing up will not help and extra space can make movement worse. Diagnose the failure first with the protective mailer comparison.

/small-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about small poly mailers

faqs.q: Why can a 9x12 cost less to ship than a 6x9 small poly mailer?
faqs.a: Small-parcel rates often depend on depth as well as footprint. A 9x12 lets a folded item lie flat and thin, while the same item forced into a 6x9 bunches into a thicker lump that can cross into a higher rate. Check that the packed parcel is flat.

faqs.q: Do small poly mailers need heavy film?
faqs.a: Rarely, unless the contents have hard corners. Soft accessories and small garments put little stress on film. A boxed item in a tight small bag pushes a corner against the film, so size up or use a cushioned format for those.

faqs.q: How much branding fits on small poly mailers?
faqs.a: Less than most brands expect. A wordmark, strapline and social handles will not read on a small panel. One mark, sized properly, does more, and one side printed well usually beats two sides printed tightly.

faqs.q: Are colored small poly mailers good value for branding?
faqs.a: Yes. Small parcels arrive in a stack with others, and color separates yours before anything is opened. Colored film costs far less than a printed run, so small formats are where it gives the most impact for the least spend.

faqs.q: Should subscription brands add a tear tab to small poly mailers?
faqs.a: It is worth considering. On gift and subscription ranges the opening is part of the experience, and a tear tab means no scissors. It also helps keep a returns strip intact if you specify a double-strip closure.

faqs.q: Can I get samples of both small poly mailer sizes to compare?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us what goes in the parcel, including inserts, and we will recommend a size, quote it and send samples if that helps you decide. Compare fit notes on the 6x9 poly mailers page as well.

/sustainability/.h2: More questions about our sustainability position

faqs.q: Why is there no certification mark on The Poly Mailers sustainability position?
faqs.a: A certification mark states that an assessment happened, and we hold no documentation for one, so we do not display one. The same applies to recycled percentages, breakdown periods and carbon comparisons: none was supplied with evidence, so none is published.

faqs.q: How does the sustainability evidence process work for my mailer order?
faqs.a: You tell us what you need to say, we go to the supplier of the specific film for your order, and we ask for feedstock, proportion, assessment method, assessing body and the document. You see the answer before committing, and what is evidenced goes on the quotation.

faqs.q: What happens under the sustainability process if no evidence exists?
faqs.a: You are told before you order. When the film supplier cannot document a claim, that answer is information too, and it lets you change the claim, the material or the wording on the bag rather than discovering the gap after printing.

faqs.q: Why is right-sizing central to the poly mailer sustainability position?
faqs.a: A parcel that fits uses less film, weighs less and takes less vehicle space, and unlike a material claim it can be measured in your own data within a month. It is the largest lever most operations have and needs no certificate to defend.

faqs.q: How does a returns strip support poly mailer sustainability goals?
faqs.a: A resealable mailer removes an entire second piece of packaging from every return. In categories with high return rates, that is a substantial share of total packaging material, and the reduction is measurable from your own order and returns data.

faqs.q: How should I compare sustainability sections in supplier mailer quotes?
faqs.a: Ask each supplier for the feedstock type, the proportion, the assessment method and the document, and see who can produce all four. A confident percentage without evidence says a lot about a quote. Use the sustainable terminology guide for wording.

/sustainable-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about sustainable poly mailer options

faqs.q: Which sustainable poly mailer option is easiest to defend this quarter?
faqs.a: Recycled content is the practical starting point. It is backed by a declaration or certificate and does not depend on what disposal facilities your customer can reach. The other two routes are worth pursuing once documentation and infrastructure both exist.

faqs.q: What do compostable poly mailers need to deliver their benefit?
faqs.a: A composting process your customer can actually reach. Compostable is a disposal claim with the strongest story and the hardest execution, so check that a suitable route exists where your customers live before promising it on the bag.

faqs.q: Why are biodegradable poly mailers the riskiest sustainable option to claim?
faqs.a: Biodegradable is the least defined term and is difficult to support without named conditions and a timeframe. It carries the most claim risk for a brand printing it, which is why the other two routes are usually safer starting points.

faqs.q: Can sustainable poly mailer goals be met without changing material?
faqs.a: Yes. Right-sizing, removing components such as inserts and second bags, specifying a returns strip and printing accurate disposal wording all reduce impact measurably. None needs a certification, and each can be evidenced from your own operation.

faqs.q: What disposal wording should go on sustainable poly mailers?
faqs.a: Wording that is true where your customers live. An accurate instruction on where the film can be taken gets followed, while a generic symbol usually does not. Check the wording for each market you sell into before approving the proof.

faqs.q: Why does the sustainable poly mailer comparison publish no percentages?
faqs.a: None were supplied with evidence. Recycled content varies by film, batch and market, so a single figure could not be honored for every order. We confirm what the film for your order supports, in writing, with the documentation behind it.

faqs.q: What should I send to compare sustainable poly mailer options?
faqs.a: Tell us what you need to claim and which markets you sell into. We will come back with what the available film supports. Start with the recycled poly mailer details if documented feedstock is your priority.

/uk/.h2: More questions about poly mailers for UK customers

faqs.q: Are polythene mailing bags and poly mailers the same in the UK?
faqs.a: Yes. Polythene mailing bags, mailing pouches and plastic postal envelopes usually describe the same product this site calls poly mailers. If you are unsure, send a photograph of what you currently use, which settles it faster than vocabulary.

faqs.q: Why does parcel thickness matter so much for UK mailer orders?
faqs.a: UK small-parcel pricing is unusually sensitive to thickness, because format thresholds are built around it. For businesses sending small items in volume, sizing to stay inside a letterbox band is often a bigger cost lever than anything else in the specification.

faqs.q: Is there UK stock available for a fast top-up of mailers?
faqs.a: No. There are no UK premises, trade counter or local stock, so every order is made to the specification you approve and shipped to your address. Plan against the schedule confirmed in writing on your quotation rather than a quick restock.

faqs.q: How is a delivery schedule set for a UK poly mailer order?
faqs.a: It is confirmed in writing for your specific order rather than published as a general figure, because production and transit depend on specification, quantity and proof approval. Tell us any fixed date at the start so the schedule is built around it.

faqs.q: Do UK delivery access limits affect a poly mailer order?
faqs.a: They can. Mention access constraints such as upper floors, restricted streets or limited unloading space at quotation stage, and the delivery can be arranged around them. Delivery arrangements to some Scottish addresses also differ from the rest of the UK.

faqs.q: Which UK location pages cover specific shipping situations?
faqs.a: Each covers a different situation: London for postal thresholds, Birmingham for trade shipping, Manchester for burst demand, Leeds for store fulfillment and Glasgow for remote addresses. Start with London postal format thresholds for small parcels.

/usa/.h2: More questions about poly mailers for US customers

faqs.q: How should US businesses structure a first poly mailer order?
faqs.a: Start with samples to settle size, then place a modest first run rather than a year of stock, and move to volume once the specification has proved itself in your own operation. That sequence keeps a new supplier relationship low risk.

faqs.q: Can US buyers get a next-day poly mailer delivery?
faqs.a: No. Orders are made to the specification you approve and shipped to your address, so there is no shelf stock for same-week or next-day top-ups. A schedule is confirmed in writing for your order, so you plan against a real date.

faqs.q: Is the specification process the same for US poly mailer orders as elsewhere?
faqs.a: Yes. Specification, proofing and quality checks are the same wherever the order goes. What differs for US customers is that you order to a schedule, with the currency, documentation and delivery arrangements confirmed in writing.

faqs.q: Do US location pages cover different shipping problems?
faqs.a: Yes. Each covers a distinct situation, such as Texas heat and storage, Seattle rain, Denver altitude, Virginia returns or New York City mailrooms, rather than repeating the same content with a new place name. Pick the one closest to your operation.

faqs.q: Is the phone number for US poly mailer customers a local number?
faqs.a: No. The contact line serves every market and is not presented as a local US number, because it is not one. Either phone line reaches the same team, and anything agreed by phone is confirmed back to you in writing.

faqs.q: What should US businesses settle before requesting a poly mailer price?
faqs.a: What goes in the parcel, quantity over time, sizes, print, color, finish, closure, protection needs, delivery address type and the date stock is needed. Work through the custom mailer ordering checklist before contacting anyone.

/white-poly-mailers/.h2: More questions about white poly mailers

faqs.q: Why are white poly mailers best for a first printed run?
faqs.a: White accepts every ink color, so artwork moves from file to proof without solving contrast problems or redesigning. Gradients hold, photographs reproduce and pale tones stay pale, which makes white the least risky surface for a first run.

faqs.q: When is a colored base better than white poly mailers?
faqs.a: If your identity is a single mark in one color, a colored base gives more recognition for less. Mostly solid designs can also look more even on a colored film, because large solids on white show any inconsistency in ink lay-down.

faqs.q: Does matte finish help white poly mailers hide scuffs?
faqs.a: Yes, noticeably. White shows conveyor marks, ink transfer and grip lines, and a matte finish disguises them better than gloss. A design that carries interest across the panel, rather than leaving large clean areas, also helps.

faqs.q: Do white poly mailers suit brands with several sub-brands?
faqs.a: They do. One white film can carry different artwork for each line, so you manage a single base material rather than a separate color for every sub-brand. It keeps stock simpler while each range still looks distinct.

faqs.q: Are white poly mailers good for hand-written or large labels?
faqs.a: Yes. White gives labels and pen the contrast they need, which helps operations that hand-write addresses or apply large shipping labels. Labels also read clearly for scanning against a plain white panel.

faqs.q: How are white poly mailer print runs checked for quality?
faqs.a: White shows registration drift, color variation and speckling clearly, so it is easy to inspect. Proofs are checked against approved artwork at intervals through the run, not just at the start. Compare unprinted options on blank poly mailers.

/locations/georgia/.h2: More questions from growing Georgia brands

faqs.q: Should a Georgia brand pay for a custom color match yet?
faqs.a: Usually not at the growth stage. A stock color close to your brand looks the same to a customer who has never seen your swatch, at a fraction of the cost, so a custom match is worth deferring until volume and artwork have settled.

faqs.q: Is full-coverage printing a sensible first run for Georgia businesses?
faqs.a: Rarely. A single mark on a colored base is a cheaper first printed run, and it teaches you what customers actually respond to. Full coverage can follow once you know which parts of the design earn their place on the parcel.

faqs.q: Should Georgia sellers buy a full year of mailer stock at once?
faqs.a: The volume discount is real, but so is the risk that the specification turns out wrong halfway through the year. While your range is still moving, ordering a season at a time keeps you from storing bags you no longer want.

faqs.q: Does a growing Georgia product range really need a fourth mailer size?
faqs.a: Most ranges that think they need four sizes need three, plus a plain oversized bag for the occasional outlier. Each extra size adds a decision at the packing bench, and decisions made under time pressure are where packing errors start.

faqs.q: Which mailers suit Georgia film and entertainment merchandise with sharp demand peaks?
faqs.a: Production-linked merchandise sells in short, sharp bursts, so committing to large printed runs ahead of each release is risky. Blank or colored stock in a standard size such as 10x13 covers the peak without leaving branded dead stock once demand drops away.

faqs.q: How should Georgia beauty and haircare brands protect fragile product cartons?
faqs.a: Beauty and haircare carry the same fragile-carton problem everywhere: a printed retail box scuffs or crushes inside a plain film bag. Where the carton is part of what the customer receives, bubble-lined poly mailers protect it better than a heavier film alone.

faqs.q: What is a low-commitment way for Georgia brands to look branded?
faqs.a: Colored poly mailers with a printed sticker get most of the recognition benefit of a printed run for a fraction of the commitment. That approach suits the stage where monthly volume still swings and the artwork is still changing, which describes many Georgia growth-stage businesses.

/locations/illinois/.h2: More questions from Illinois distribution buyers

faqs.q: Why do gussets matter for Illinois parcels moving between facilities?
faqs.a: A parcel that sits flat and square travels in a cage without being crushed by the ones stacked on top. When a shipment will be consolidated, broken down and reshipped through Illinois distribution, a gusseted bag that holds its shape earns its cost at every stage.

faqs.q: How do label problems multiply on parcels routed through Illinois hubs?
faqs.a: A label lifting at the edges causes an exception at every later facility, not just one. Apply labels to a flat panel away from folds and seals, so the barcode reads cleanly each time the parcel is scanned on its way through the network.

faqs.q: Should Illinois shippers consolidate multi-item orders into one large mailer?
faqs.a: Often, because every unnecessary cubic inch is paid for more than once when shipments move between facilities. Weigh a packed sample first, since one consolidated parcel can cross a weight band that two smaller ones stayed below. Our 19x24 consolidation poly mailers cover the larger format.

faqs.q: Which mailers suit Illinois trade printers shipping flat and rigid goods?
faqs.a: Flat printed goods need enough footprint to lie flat without bending at the edges, and rigid items need a fit close enough that they cannot slide around inside the bag. Send the finished dimensions and we will size against the item rather than a chart.

faqs.q: What should Illinois food and specialty producers check before choosing a mailer?
faqs.a: Contents in this category are often heavier than they look, so weigh a packed parcel rather than judging by size. Weight affects which film is appropriate and which carrier band the parcel falls into, and both are easier to settle on a sample.

faqs.q: How should Illinois packers seal mailers that will be sorted repeatedly?
faqs.a: Press the full length of the adhesive strip, not just the center. Each handling is another chance for a partial bond to open, and parcels passing through Illinois consolidation points are handled far more often than a straight local delivery.

faqs.q: Why do Illinois fulfillment operations standardize on 10x13 poly mailers?
faqs.a: National fulfillment operations located centrally to cut average transit distance tend to settle on 10x13 because it covers a wide spread of everyday orders with one bag. A single standard size also keeps bench decisions simple when volume is high.

/locations/indiana/.h2: More questions from Indiana controlled supply chains

faqs.q: Why should Indiana buyers keep a reference sample from each run?
faqs.a: A bag kept from each accepted run is the reference against which any future question is settled. If a repeat order looks or behaves differently, you can compare it directly with the sample rather than relying on memory or a written description.

faqs.q: Can Indiana buyers test a changed film before committing to a run?
faqs.a: Yes. Where a change in film is material, a sample is available first so you can test it against your own contents before committing. Nothing is substituted quietly, and the specification on the quotation matches what will actually be produced.

faqs.q: Why should Indiana controlled supply chains specify the closure explicitly?
faqs.a: The closure is the component most affected by a material change, so naming it explicitly protects the part most likely to behave differently. Self-seal adhesive and strip type are worth stating on the quotation rather than leaving to whatever film happens to be available.

faqs.q: How should Indiana buyers specify an exact count requirement?
faqs.a: Say so at inquiry stage. Manufactured runs do not stop at an exact unit, and a tolerance applies either side of the ordered figure, so an exact count has to be specified rather than discovered on delivery. Our custom order policy explains how tolerance is stated.

faqs.q: What should Indiana buyers ask a supplier about possible film changes?
faqs.a: Ask what would change if the film moved: strength, seal behavior, print, or nothing at all. A supplier who can answer that has thought about your problem. We describe any difference plainly rather than minimizing it, so you can judge its effect.

faqs.q: Why do Indiana manufacturers often choose blank mailers in common sizes?
faqs.a: Every option you specify is something that can become unavailable later. A plain bag in a widely available size and standard film has the fewest failure points, which makes it the safest choice for B2B shipping where specification consistency is a requirement.

faqs.q: What do Indiana regulated supply chains need from a packaging supplier?
faqs.a: Operations where an input change has to be documented rather than absorbed need notice before anything different ships, a plain description of what changed, and a quotation stating the exact specification produced. Tell us at quotation stage that consistency is a requirement, not a preference.

/locations/indianapolis/.h2: More questions from Indianapolis fulfillment teams

faqs.q: How can an Indianapolis business test whether its mailers are over-specified?
faqs.a: Look at your damage rate by product, then quote the specification below your current one alongside it. Run a controlled batch of a few thousand parcels on the lighter film, tracked separately, and compare the damage rate against the saving before changing everything.

faqs.q: Why check damage by product line before downgrading Indianapolis packaging?
faqs.a: An overall damage figure hides where the problem actually sits. If damage clusters in one product line, the current specification may be right for everything else, and only that line needs attention rather than a change of film across the whole range.

faqs.q: Which Indianapolis products should stay on a heavier poly mailer film?
faqs.a: Anything with hard corners, anything heavy for its size, and anything shipping beyond your regional core argue for keeping the heavier film. A lighter specification only makes sense where the failure it protects against is genuinely absent from your parcels.

faqs.q: When is a lighter film saving genuinely free for Indianapolis shippers?
faqs.a: When the damage rate on a tracked trial batch does not move. If it moves at all, work out whether the arithmetic still holds once replacements are counted. Our economy poly mailer specification sets out how to make that calculation.

faqs.q: Why do Indianapolis fulfillment benches favor self-seal poly mailers?
faqs.a: When transits are short and handling events are few, bench speed matters more than extra protection. A self-seal strip closes in one motion, saving seconds per parcel across national fulfillment volumes, provided packers still press the full length of the strip.

faqs.q: Should Indianapolis fulfillment operations use branded or blank poly mailers?
faqs.a: Where the operation is fulfillment rather than brand-led, blank poly mailers are usually the practical choice. They avoid artwork approval and keep the specification simple, which matters when the main goal is moving parcels quickly across the country.

faqs.q: What should Indianapolis businesses send to get a comparison quote?
faqs.a: Send your current specification and your damage rate. We will quote the level below it alongside your current one, so you can compare both in real numbers and decide whether a lighter film is worth a trial before changing your whole order.

/locations/jacksonville/.h2: More questions from Jacksonville import operations

faqs.q: Do goods arriving inner-packed in Jacksonville need extra packaging?
faqs.a: Goods that arrive individually bagged need nothing beyond the outbound mailer. Goods that arrive loose need two layers, an inner bag and the mailer, so finding out how a container is packed before it lands saves deciding parcel by parcel at the bench.

faqs.q: Should Jacksonville importers size mailers against the case or the unit?
faqs.a: Against the single unit a customer receives. The inbound case format was decided by somebody else, often on another continent, and tells you nothing about the outbound requirement, so measure the individual item as it will be packed.

faqs.q: How should Jacksonville operations store mailer cartons in the local climate?
faqs.a: Keep them sealed, off the floor, away from external walls and out of direct light. Heat and humidity age the closure adhesive rather than the film, as our guide to humidity and seasonality in Florida explains in more detail.

faqs.q: Why do Jacksonville third-party fulfillment operations use blank poly mailers?
faqs.a: Breaking down imported stock for several brand clients rules out branding on the outer bag. Blank mailers in a small set of standard sizes let one bench serve every client without holding separate printed stock for each of them.

faqs.q: When do economy poly mailers make sense for Jacksonville break-bulk operations?
faqs.a: Where packaging is a per-unit line in a high-throughput operation, the film cost repeats on every parcel leaving the building. Economy mailers suit goods that arrive inner-packed and have no hard corners, so the lighter film is not asked to do protective work.

faqs.q: Which mailer suits Jacksonville outbound volume going to trade customers?
faqs.a: 19x24 poly mailers suit the portion of outbound volume that goes to trade rather than to consumers, where several units travel together in one parcel. Consumer orders broken down to single items usually fit the 10x13 outbound standard instead.

faqs.q: What should Jacksonville importers tell you to get an outbound range specified?
faqs.a: Tell us what arrives in the container and what a customer receives at the other end. We will specify the smallest outbound range that covers the gap, usually two or three sizes with written rules for which bag each item goes in.

/locations/london/.h2: More questions from London small-item sellers

faqs.q: Why does parcel thickness matter more than weight for London shipments?
faqs.a: UK postal pricing has a format band for items that fit through a letterbox, set at a specific thickness. Crossing it moves a parcel into a different pricing band and can affect first-time delivery, so depth is often a bigger cost lever than weight.

faqs.q: Where should London sellers check current letterbox format thresholds?
faqs.a: With your carrier directly. Thresholds are reviewed periodically, so rely on the carrier's current figures rather than a number published anywhere else, including on our site. Then measure a real packed parcel against them instead of estimating from product dimensions.

faqs.q: How should London fashion sellers fold garments to stay letterbox-friendly?
faqs.a: Fold each item to a flat rectangle. An irregular bundle has a thick point, and the thick point is what gets measured. A wider mailer that lets the garment lie flat usually keeps it thinner than squeezing it into a smaller bag.

faqs.q: Can inserts push a London parcel out of the letterbox band?
faqs.a: Yes. A folded card, a sample and a returns slip together can add the millimeters that cross a threshold. Rethink what goes in the parcel, then measure the packed result again before committing to a mailer format for the whole range.

faqs.q: Which poly mailer sizes suit London jewelry and cosmetics sellers?
faqs.a: Small items such as jewelry, cosmetics and accessories can realistically stay inside a letterbox format, and 6x9 poly mailers are the format most likely to keep them there. Our small poly mailer formats compare the options when thickness is the constraint.

faqs.q: Which mailer suits London publishers and printers sending flat goods?
faqs.a: Flat goods need footprint without gaining thickness, which is what 9x12 poly mailers provide. With print and publishing, the item itself usually decides the thickness question, so the mailer's job is to lie flat around it without adding bulk.

faqs.q: What if a London product cannot fit through a letterbox at all?
faqs.a: Accept that it is a parcel rather than forcing the attempt, which tends to cost more. The decision then shifts back to fit and protection rather than thickness, and the right size comes from packing a sample into two candidate mailers.

/locations/manchester/.h2: More questions from Manchester campaign retailers

faqs.q: Should Manchester retailers forecast packaging by month or by busiest day?
faqs.a: By the busiest day. A campaign or drop can ship in one day what would ordinarily take two weeks, and that number is what has to be on the bench. Packaging planned against a monthly average is exactly what runs short during a burst.

faqs.q: Why should Manchester fashion brands hold plain mailers under branded stock?
faqs.a: So a shortfall in a printed line never stops orders going out. Blank poly mailers act as fallback stock during a flash sale, and a parcel sent on time in a plain bag is far better than a branded one shipped late.

faqs.q: How should Manchester brands prepare for the returns wave after a drop?
faqs.a: Expect it roughly two weeks after the campaign, at a similar scale to the outbound burst. A double-strip closure lets customers reuse the original bag, as our closure and self-seal guide explains, so returns arrive in packaging you chose.

faqs.q: What does pre-staging packaging mean for a Manchester flash sale?
faqs.a: Opening cartons and positioning mailers at each bench before the day, not during it. On the busiest day every minute spent fetching stock or opening boxes is a minute not packing, and temporary staff work faster when everything is within reach.

faqs.q: Why do labels lift on rushed Manchester campaign parcels?
faqs.a: Under time pressure labels get stuck across folds, and a label over a fold lifts in transit and generates delivery exceptions. A simple written rule placing the label on a flat panel holds up better than relying on packers to remember during a burst.

faqs.q: Are economy poly mailers worth considering for Manchester burst volumes?
faqs.a: Often, because at burst volumes unit cost compounds faster than at any other time. If your parcels are soft fashion goods without hard corners, a lighter film can carry them safely, and the saving repeats across every parcel on the busiest day.

faqs.q: How should Manchester music and event merchandise sellers seal parcels?
faqs.a: Music and event-linked merchandise sells in spikes around releases and dates, much like a fashion drop. Self-seal poly mailers matter most then, because seconds per parcel count on the busiest day, provided packers press the strip fully rather than folding it.

/locations/maryland/.h2: More questions from Maryland institutional buyers

faqs.q: Can Maryland nonprofits get mailers specified to a fixed budget?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us the budget rather than just the quantity, and we can specify to that figure instead of quoting something that has to go back for re-approval. Economy poly mailers are often the starting point when the budget sets the specification.

faqs.q: Who should sign the proof for a Maryland institutional printed order?
faqs.a: Name the approver at the start, particularly if the person signing the proof is not the person who chose the specification. A proof that waits for someone new to the order takes longer, and that delay usually lands right before a deadline.

faqs.q: How can Maryland organizations avoid a rushed order at budget year end?
faqs.a: Ask for a quotation ahead of the deadline rather than into it. Budget cycles and delivery dates rarely align on their own, so planning the order before year end gives the schedule room instead of forcing a compressed proof and production window.

faqs.q: When should Maryland buyers raise sustainability or accessibility documentation requirements?
faqs.a: At the start, before the quotation is issued, because requirements raised later are harder to satisfy. We provide whatever exists for the specific film supplied and say plainly when something does not, as our position on sustainability documentation sets out.

faqs.q: Which mailer suits Maryland member packs and publication mailings?
faqs.a: 9x12 poly mailers suit publications, document packs and member mailings, giving flat contents enough room without excess film. Where contents vary between sends, a 10x13 mailer covers more variation with a single line on the purchase order.

faqs.q: Why do Maryland institutions often order blank poly mailers on purchase orders?
faqs.a: Blank mailers are the simplest line to specify on a purchase order because there is no artwork approval in the chain. That removes a whole sign-off step, which matters when an approval cycle already involves several people and a fixed budget window.

faqs.q: How should Maryland advocacy groups time campaign mailings against a fixed date?
faqs.a: Nonprofit and advocacy mailings often carry a fixed budget and a fixed send date. Tell us the date the mailers must arrive when you ask for a price, and the production schedule, including when proof approval becomes critical, is confirmed in writing.

/locations/melbourne/.h2: More questions from Melbourne independent labels

faqs.q: Are frosted garment bags worth it for Melbourne fashion labels?
faqs.a: For a label whose product justifies it, yes. A bagged garment arrives presented rather than loose, stays clean, and leaves the customer a resealable bag. Our frosted garment presentation bags cost less than printing the outer and do more visible work.

faqs.q: How can a Melbourne label brand parcels without printing the mailer?
faqs.a: Use colored or black stock with a printed seal. The seal carries your mark, the mailer color does the visual work, and nothing is committed a season ahead, which suits labels whose range moves with each small production batch.

faqs.q: Which mailer finish photographs best for Melbourne brands sharing unboxing images?
faqs.a: Matte finishes and considered colors photograph evenly without styling. Gloss white needs careful lighting to look right, so if customers or your own team photograph parcels for social channels, a matte surface saves effort on every shot.

faqs.q: How should Melbourne fashion labels plan mailers for sizing returns?
faqs.a: Sizing returns are certain in fashion at any scale, so choose a mailer with a double-strip closure that customers can reseal to send items back. That avoids a second bag in the parcel and keeps returns arriving in your own packaging.

faqs.q: What should Melbourne craft and homeware makers prioritize in a mailer?
faqs.a: Makers selling direct through their own channels share the fashion labels' tension: high standards at modest volume. Prioritize a mailer that matches the standard of the piece and fits it closely, then add branding through a printed seal rather than a printed run.

faqs.q: Is light pink an option for Melbourne labels with a softer palette?
faqs.a: Yes. Light pink poly mailers offer a tonal option for labels whose palette is softer than black. Ask for a sample to view next to your product, because a mailer color reads differently beside a real garment than it does on a screen.

faqs.q: What should Melbourne independent beauty brands spend on first?
faqs.a: Judge each option by presentation gained per dollar spent. At small quantities a colored or black mailer with a printed seal usually comes before a printed outer, which stays high per unit at this scale and is hard to justify until volumes grow.

/locations/michigan/.h2: More questions from Michigan industrial shippers

faqs.q: How should Michigan parts suppliers package parcels going to a loading dock?
faqs.a: A dock parcel arrives with others, is signed for and is opened by someone doing a job, so it is judged on intact, identifiable contents. Legible identification matters more than a logo, containment more than cushioning, and stacking more than appearance.

faqs.q: When is a poly mailer the wrong choice for Michigan industrial shipments?
faqs.a: Anything rigid, crush-sensitive or with a sharp protrusion is better served by a carton, and adding film weight will not change that. Work out which failure you have first, using our protective mailer comparison guide.

faqs.q: Why is film weight a serious decision for Michigan automotive parts shippers?
faqs.a: A damaged consumer order costs a replacement and some goodwill, but a damaged part can stop a production line. That changes the arithmetic, so film weight for automotive and aftermarket components is chosen for containment and performance rather than unit cost.

faqs.q: Which poly mailer size suits a mixed Michigan parts range?
faqs.a: 12x15 poly mailers are the mid-size that absorbs the most variation in a mixed parts range. Pairing it with a small set of other controlled sizes keeps the specification stable while covering most components without wasting film.
