faqs.q: Can Michigan contract manufacturers order mailers to a customer's written specification?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the specification and we will quote against it, stating film, weight, closure, dimensions and tolerance on the quotation rather than describing them in conversation. That written record is what a contract manufacturer needs to show its own customer.

faqs.q: Do Michigan B2B shipments need presentation-grade poly mailers?
faqs.a: Rarely. Shipping into other businesses seldom needs presentation, so the decision is about performance and cost. Economy or blank poly mailers in controlled sizes are what most industrial flows run on, with film weight chosen against the parts being shipped.

faqs.q: How do Michigan direct-selling apparel brands differ from industrial mailer buyers?
faqs.a: Apparel and merchandise sold direct is judged at the doorstep rather than the dock, so fit and presentation matter where they would not on a parts shipment. Businesses running both flows usually do better with two mailer lines than one compromise.

/locations/minnesota/.h2: More questions from Minnesota retail suppliers

faqs.q: What should Minnesota retail suppliers send for an accurate mailer quote?
faqs.a: Send the retailer's packaging document itself rather than a summary. Permitted formats, required printed information, labeling position, bag and case quantities and perforation requirements all affect what can be quoted, and details lost in a summary cause problems later.

faqs.q: Do Minnesota retail specifications require perforated or vented poly bags?
faqs.a: Some do. Specifications for bags containing consumer goods can include vent or suffocation-warning requirements, so check the retailer's document and send it to us. We quote exactly what it calls for rather than assuming a standard bag will pass.

faqs.q: Can a Minnesota retailer's labeling position rule out mailer artwork?
faqs.a: Yes. Labeling position and size are frequently prescribed, and the reserved area can rule out artwork on a whole panel. That is one reason retail supply usually runs on blank mailers, with any brand design kept for a separate direct line.

faqs.q: Why is changing an accepted retail packaging specification hard in Minnesota?
faqs.a: Once a retail buyer accepts a specification, changing it becomes an administrative exercise rather than a purchasing decision. Consistency across reorders is worth more than a marginal saving, and our custom order policy explains how material changes are handled.

faqs.q: Which mailer format do Minnesota retailers most commonly accept?
faqs.a: Where a poly bag is permitted at all, 10x13 poly mailers are the format most commonly accepted. Check first that the retailer allows a poly bag for your product category, because that is not universal, and confirm any prescribed bag and case quantities.

faqs.q: What do Minnesota medical and health product suppliers need alongside mailers?
faqs.a: The sector carries strong documentation habits, so expect to need material information for your records as well as the bags. Tell us at inquiry stage, and we will provide what exists for the specific film supplied and say plainly where nothing is documented.

faqs.q: Why do Minnesota retail suppliers compare economy mailers once the format is fixed?
faqs.a: When the retailer prescribes the format, cost per unit becomes the remaining variable. Economy poly mailers can satisfy a fixed specification at a lower unit cost, provided the film still meets everything the retailer's document requires.

/locations/montreal/.h2: More questions from Montreal bilingual brands

faqs.q: How can Montreal brands fit two languages on one poly mailer?
faqs.a: Split them across faces, with one language on the front and the other on the back. Each gets full-size type and neither is crowded, which works better on flexible film than squeezing both into a single panel with smaller lettering.

faqs.q: Why should Montreal bilingual mailers cut copy rather than shrink type?
faqs.a: On film, small type loses its counters and becomes hard to read. Cutting words is almost always better than shrinking them, and with two languages competing for the same panel, every unnecessary word costs legibility on both.

faqs.q: Can care symbols reduce wording on Montreal bilingual poly mailers?
faqs.a: Yes, where the meaning allows. Care icons and handling marks carry information without wording in either language, freeing space for copy that has to be written out. They suit apparel brands in particular, where care details would otherwise fill a panel.

faqs.q: Should Montreal businesses move detailed bilingual information onto a printed insert?
faqs.a: Often, yes. A card can carry both languages at readable size in a way a bag panel cannot, leaving the mailer for your mark and essential wording. It also keeps detailed product information from competing with the shipping label.

faqs.q: How much wording should Montreal retail brands put on a poly mailer?
faqs.a: As little as does the job. Customer-facing wording in two languages takes real space, and type cannot shrink far on film, so keep the bag to essentials. Our artwork guidelines for film printing cover the legibility limits.

faqs.q: Why do symmetrical layouts break on Montreal bilingual poly mailers?
faqs.a: The same sentence is usually longer in one language than the other, so copy roughly doubles, and unevenly. A layout built as mirrored halves rarely holds once real text goes in, which is why artwork planned around both versions beats translating afterwards.

faqs.q: Does language prominence affect Montreal poly mailer layout?
faqs.a: It can. Language rules commonly address how prominently each language appears, not only whether it is there, so a layout giving one language larger type or a better position may need rethinking. What applies to your business is a question for a qualified adviser.

/locations/ottawa/.h2: More questions from Ottawa national shippers

faqs.q: When do poly bubble mailers make sense for Ottawa national distribution?
faqs.a: For the share of volume that travels far and is handled repeatedly. A bubble lining bonded to a film outer adds impact protection and moisture resistance, which suits long routes with several transfer points and contents that would mark if knocked.

faqs.q: Why does closure quality matter so much for parcels leaving Ottawa?
faqs.a: Every consolidation and transfer point is another test of a partially pressed seal, and a cross-country parcel passes through more of them. Self-seal closures pressed along their full length matter more here, as our closure and self-seal guide explains.

faqs.q: Which failure should Ottawa distributors design their mailer specification around?
faqs.a: Ask which failure you would least like to have rather than which specification suits the average parcel. For most national distributors that is a damaged delivery to a remote address, because it is the most expensive to put right and the most visible.

faqs.q: Do Ottawa membership mailings sent across Canada need a different specification?
faqs.a: They travel the same long routes as commercial parcels, so they benefit from the same thinking. A mailer sized closely to the pack, with a film and closure chosen for the harder journeys, avoids creased or opened packs reaching remote members.

faqs.q: Why do Ottawa distribution operations often run blank poly mailers?
faqs.a: Where distribution rather than brand is the operation, blank mailers keep the specification simple and free of artwork approval. They can still be specified in a film weight and closure suited to long routes, which matters more than appearance across the country.

faqs.q: Why is a single 10x13 mailer a sensible standard for Ottawa shippers?
faqs.a: A single 10x13 standard can be specified for the harder routes without overpaying badly on the easy ones. Running one size across the whole flow keeps bench decisions simple while film and closure choices handle the variation in destinations.

faqs.q: What should Ottawa businesses send to get a national mailer specification?
faqs.a: Tell us the spread of where your parcels go, including the share heading to remote addresses. We will specify against the route you cannot afford to fail rather than the average one, with the quotation issued in Canadian dollars.

/locations/phoenix/.h2: More questions from Phoenix regional shippers

faqs.q: How do Phoenix shippers stop items marking each other on long legs?
faqs.a: Separate touching surfaces with a layer between them. Two items rubbing together for hours on a road leg will mark each other, and a simple divider is cheap compared with a return. Fit closely too, so nothing can move inside the mailer.

faqs.q: Why does seal pressing matter more for parcels leaving Phoenix?
faqs.a: Vibration over long road legs tests a seal continuously rather than once, and given enough hours it finds every part of a strip that was not properly bonded. Press the whole length of the self-seal strip, not just the middle, before dispatch.

faqs.q: Do padded mailers help Phoenix parcels on long road journeys?
faqs.a: They can, for a different reason than usual. Here the cushioning works as a buffer against sustained vibration rather than a single impact, protecting surfaces that would otherwise rub. Padded poly mailers suit items that abrade easily or carry finishes worth protecting.

faqs.q: How does the Phoenix delivery network differ from a dense city network?
faqs.a: A parcel leaving Phoenix for much of the southwest travels long legs with relatively few handling points. That means less impact damage than a dense urban network but more exposure to time, temperature and vibration, so specify for movement rather than drops.

faqs.q: Which mailers suit Phoenix outdoor and recreation retailers shipping to remote addresses?
faqs.a: Products in this category often travel long distances to remote addresses, so the priorities are a close fit, a fully pressed seal and a pale outer in summer. Where items have parts that could rub or mark, a padded mailer adds a useful buffer.

faqs.q: What should Phoenix regional distributors describe when requesting a mailer quote?
faqs.a: Tell us where your parcels travel and how long they typically spend in transit. We will specify for movement and exposure rather than impact, because long legs across a sparsely populated area produce different failures from short urban deliveries.

faqs.q: Should Phoenix brands plan heat-sensitive summer shipments beyond the mailer itself?
faqs.a: Yes. Time and temperature compound, so a parcel unaffected by an hour in a hot vehicle can be affected by six on a long leg. Anything with a melting point needs planning beyond packaging, and our Arizona heat and packaging guide covers what helps.
